Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 31, verse 12 (part 1 of 2):

Then the Truth, glory be to Him, says: ﴿And We indeed gave Luqman wisdom [saying], "Be grateful to Allah. And whoever is grateful - he is grateful only for [the benefit of] himself. And whoever is ungrateful - indeed, Allah is Free of need and Praiseworthy."﴾ (12)

The Truth, glory be to Him, gave us before He created us, and gave us after He created us the method (al-manhaj), then He sent to us the caravans of messages that carry to every environment the method that suits it. Before Adam, peace be upon him, was sent out to bear the burden of this vicegerency (khilafah), Allah gave him a trial. This trial meant that he should preserve his Lord's method in "do" and "do not do," and that he should beware of the plotting of Satan.

Adam went through this explanatory trial before Allah chose him (ijtiba') for prophethood. Many people think that Adam's disobedience came after he was charged with prophethood, and they say: How can Adam disobey his Lord when he is a prophet, and the prophet is infallible (ma'sum)?

We say: Yes, Adam disobeyed his Lord, but before prophethood, while he was still an ordinary human being. Therefore He, glory be to Him, said concerning him: ﴿And Adam disobeyed his Lord, so he erred. Then his Lord chose him, accepted his repentance, and guided him.﴾ [Ta-Ha] (121-122)

So, the choosing (ijtiba') came after the disobedience. If you say: What is the reason for the disobedience issuing from Adam, when he was being prepared for prophethood? They say: Because he is the father of mankind, and mankind is of two kinds: infallible humans, who are the prophets, and humans who have no infallibility, who are the common people other than the prophets. Adam had to represent both kinds, because he is the father of all. He represented the common humans when he fell into disobedience, and he represented the prophets when his Lord chose him and accepted his repentance. Thus he combined both aspects.

Here He, glory be to Him, says: ﴿And We indeed gave...﴾ (12) [Luqman]. The giving (ita') is applied to revelation (wahy), with a difference between them. If revelation is mentioned without qualification, it refers to revelation to a messenger, with a method from Allah. Revelation in general is known as "informing in concealment" (i'lam bi-khafa').

Among its uses is His saying concerning revelation to the angels: ﴿When your Lord revealed to the angels, "I am with you, so strengthen those who have believed..."﴾ (12) [al-Anfal].

It is also revealed to humans, He says: ﴿And We revealed to the mother of Moses, "Nurse him..."﴾ (7) [al-Qasas].

It is revealed to animals: ﴿And your Lord revealed to the bee, "Take for yourself houses in the mountains..."﴾ (68) [al-Nahl].

Also among its uses: the devils reveal to one another, from the devils of mankind or the jinn: ﴿And indeed, the devils inspire their allies to dispute with you...﴾ (121) [al-An'am].

Likewise Allah reveals to the people of goodness among the followers of the messengers: ﴿And when I revealed to the disciples, "Believe in Me and in My Messenger..."﴾ (111) [al-Ma'idah].

This is the linguistic meaning of revelation, which is "informing in concealment." If you intend the technical legal (shar'i) revelation, it is Allah's informing His messenger of His method. This definition excludes all the previous types.

The Truth, glory be to Him, expressed the general giving by His saying: ﴿And it is not for a human that Allah should speak to him except by revelation, or from behind a veil, or that He sends a messenger and he reveals by His permission what He wills...﴾ (51) [al-Shura].

Giving is also meant as inspiration (ilham), and it occurs when a person possesses a sound receiving instrument, fit to receive inspiration and the thought (khatir) from the Truth, the Exalted. The receiving instrument is not fit to receive from Allah, the Exalted, unless it is built to the specifications of the Creator, the One who made and originated it, just as the radio or television receives the broadcast. If the broadcast is cut off from you, know that your receiving device has a defect. As for the broadcast, it exists and is never cut off, and to Allah belongs the highest likeness.

He, glory be to Him, has a continuous broadcast to His servants, which is received only by one whose receiving instrument is purified and fit to receive from Allah. This instrument is not fit unless it is upon the method of "do" and "do not do." It is not fit if it is formed from the unlawful and nourished by it, because the unlawful corrupts the chemistry of the nature (fitrah) which Allah created in His servants on the day He took the covenant from them: ﴿And [recall] when your Lord took from the Children of Adam, from their loins, their descendants and made them testify concerning themselves, "Am I not your Lord?" They said, "Yes..."﴾ (172) [al-A'raf].

So these descendants, if they had remained in their state of purity on the day they were in the loins of Adam and the day Allah took the covenant from them, and if they had adhered to their Lord's method in "do" and "do not do," they would have been fit for Allah's inspiration, because their receiving instrument from Allah would be sound.

Consider Allah's revelation to the mother of Moses: ﴿"Nurse him. But when you fear for him, cast him into the river and do not fear or grieve..."﴾ (7) [al-Qasas].

What receiving instrument is this, that received this command and carried it out without debating it, and felt at ease with it before she had thought about it? And how would a mother be convinced that certain death would save her infant from a suspected death?

Therefore we say: When inspiration meets a sound receiving instrument, there is nothing in the soul that rejects it or seeks evidence for it. So the mother of Moses rose and carried out the command as it was cast to her. This is the giving.

From it also is His saying: ﴿So they found a servant from among Our servants, whom We had given mercy from Us and taught him knowledge from Us﴾ (65) [al-Kahf]. The righteous servant (al-'abd al-salih) (2) was not a prophet, yet Allah gave him directly, without an intermediary, and so he became a teacher to the prophet. This was only because he was a servant of Allah upon the method of Moses, and he was sincere to Allah, the Exalted, so Allah gave him from His own presence.

And read the saying of Allah, the Exalted: ﴿O you who have believed, if you fear Allah, He will grant you a criterion (furqan)...﴾ (29) [al-Anfal]. And He, glory be to Him, said: ﴿And those who are guided, He increases them in guidance and gives them their piety.﴾ (17) [Muhammad].

So: all that is incumbent upon us, to take the inspirations of the Truth, glory be to Him, is that we preserve the purity of the constitution which Allah created, so that it remains with the specifications of its Creator. Then we walk with it upon His method, exalted is He, in "do" and "do not do." Our master Luqman was of this pure, clean, and unsullied kind, whose body was not mixed with the unlawful, and who did not neglect his Lord's method. Therefore Allah gave him wisdom (hikmah) (wisdom here means sound judgment and insight), and He said concerning him: ﴿And We indeed gave Luqman wisdom...﴾ (12).

The scholars differed about him: was he a prophet or not? The prevailing view is that he was not a prophet, because those who claim his prophethood have no sound chain of transmission (sanad). The majority agree that he was a righteous man of refined sensitivity and precise perception. Sensation, as we said, is the first basis of knowledge, and Luqman did not pass over things except with this refined sensitivity and deep, precise perception. Therefore refined perceptions and subtle sensations formed in him, which fermented in his soul, and a collection of virtues and values gathered in him that governed the movement of his life. He found happiness in himself, and he also made others around him happy with the appropriate logic and good expression he possessed. So was Luqman.

There are scholarly discussions about Luqman's personality and nationality. Some of them held that he was black, thick-lipped, like the people of southern Africa, but nonetheless white of heart and pure of inner secret, from between whose thick lips came delicate wisdom and subtle meanings.

The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, spoke the truth when he said: "Indeed Allah does not look at your bodies or your forms, but He looks at your hearts."

Therefore, when you see someone who is less than you in wealth, health, status, or appearance, do not be deceived by that. Look and reflect on what he has that distinguishes him over you. For the Creator, glory be to Him, as we said, distributed His bounty among His servants equally, so that the total of each person equals the total of the other, and there is no preference among the groups except through piety: "There is no virtue for an Arab over a non-Arab except by piety and righteous deeds."

As for those who like to divide professions, for example, into noble professions and base ones, we say: There is no base profession as long as society needs it and the movement of life cannot be upright without it. So how do you despise it, and how do you despise its people? By Allah, if the ministers sat in their homes for a week, nothing would happen. But if the sanitation workers or the sewage workers stopped for just one day, a problem would arise, and the world would become (kharrarah, i.e., a state of chaos).

How can we despise these professions and despise their people, when they are content with little and endure what others cannot bear? How can we despise them, when Allah, the Exalted, says: ﴿O you who have believed, let not a people ridicule [another] people; perhaps they may be better than them.﴾ (11) [al-Hujurat].

If you say: Since he was not a prophet, how did Allah give him? We say: By the support and inspiration about which Allah said: ﴿If you fear Allah, He will grant you a criterion﴾ (29) [al-Anfal]. Whoever preserves the specifications of his constitution according to Allah's standard takes directly from Allah.

It is like when your son asks you for a sum of money to trade with in the market, so you give him a small amount to test him with. If he succeeds and his trade makes a profit, your heart is reassured and you increase for him many times what you gave the first time. Likewise, if a person keeps good company with his Lord, Allah keeps His favor upon him and continues His overflow to him.

Therefore our master 'Umar ibn 'Abd al-'Aziz (8) said: "Nothing has fallen short for us in knowledge of what we do not know except our not acting upon what we have learned." He meant: If he were fit for increase, He would have increased us. If we were trusted with what we know, and we put it into the movement of our lives, illuminating overflows and gifts from our Lord would come to us, flowing without end. But if we take knowledge and cast it aside and do not act by it, what is the reason for more increase, when you have not benefited from what you already have?

Just as the scholars spoke about Luqman's personality and nationality, they also spoke about his wisdom. One of them asked him, after he had become familiar with him in conversation: "Were you not a slave serving so-and-so?" He said: "Yes." He asked: "So by what were you given wisdom?" He said: "By my respect for the greatness of my Lord, my fulfilment of trust in the work I was entrusted with, my truthfulness in speech, and my not involving myself in what does not concern me."

These qualities are sufficient to be a method for every believer, and to enable its possessor to speak with wisdom. By Allah, if he had only the quality of truthfulness in speech, it would have been sufficient.

Therefore Luqman reached this rank while being a black slave, so Allah gave him wisdom directly, though he was neither a prophet nor a messenger. One of the surahs of the Qur'an was named after him. This shows you that if a person is upright with Allah and sincere in His obedience, Allah gives him from His vast overflow, and he will have a remembrance among the ranks of the messengers and prophets.

It is related from Luqman's wisdom that his master ordered him to slaughter a sheep for him and bring him the two best morsels from it. So he slaughtered the sheep and brought him the heart and the tongue. On the next day, his master said: "Slaughter a sheep for me and bring me the two most wicked morsels from it." So he again brought him the heart and the tongue. He asked him: "Did you not bring me these two yesterday as the two best morsels of the sheep?" He said: "Yes. There is nothing better than them when they are good, and nothing more wicked than them when they are wicked."

After Luqman, our master, the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, came to teach us this lesson, saying: "...Indeed, in the body there is a morsel which, if it is sound, the whole body is sound, and if it is corrupt, the whole body is corrupt. Indeed, it is the heart."

He, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, says in another hadith: "Whoever guards what is between his two jaws (lihyayn) and what is between his two legs will enter Paradise."

It is related that Luqman used to give fatwas (legal opinions) to the people, and they trusted his words. This was before the time of David, peace be upon him. When David came, Luqman refrained from giving fatwas. When they asked him: "Why have you abstained from giving fatwas?" He said, and this too is from his wisdom: "Shall I not be content when I have been relieved?"

That is: Why should I cling to it, when Allah has sent someone to carry it on my behalf? He knows full well that I am merely a righteous servant (that is, he took wisdom from their dwellings, as it is said). As for David, he is a messenger from Allah. It is part of wisdom that space should be made for him, and that the field of fatwa among the people should be left to him, perhaps he will bring something better than what Luqman has. Therefore he left it to him willingly and with a good heart.

Some say: Allah gave him a choice between being a prophet or a wise man, so he said: "Since You have given me the choice, O Lord..."

(1) Luqman, peace be upon him, was an Abyssinian slave and a carpenter. This was stated by Ibn 'Abbas, in what al-Imam Ahmad related from him in al-Zuhd, and Ibn Abi Shaybah and others. Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab said: Luqman, peace be upon him, was blacker than the Sudanese of Egypt, with thick lips; Allah gave him wisdom and withheld prophethood from him. Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim related it in their tafsirs. al-Suyuti cited these reports in al-Durr al-Manthur (6/509, 510). al-Qurtubi said: He is Luqman ibn Ba'ura ibn Nahur ibn Tarih. Wahb ibn Munabbih said: He was the son of Job's sister. Muqatil said: It is mentioned that he was the son of Job's maternal aunt. See Tafsir al-Qurtubi (7/5316).

(2) Ibn Kathir said in his tafsir (3/92): "This is al-Khidr, peace be upon him, as the authentic hadiths from the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, indicate." al-Bukhari (3402), Ahmad, al-Tirmidhi (3151), and Ibn Abi Hatim related from Abu Hurayrah, from the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, that he said: "He was only named al-Khidr because he sat on a white fur, and behold, it shook beneath him and became green." al-Suyuti cited it in al-Durr al-Manthur (5/420). Ibn Hajar said in Fath al-Bari (6/434): "al-Tabari said in his History: al-Khidr was in the days of Afridun, according to the view of the general scholars of the earlier Book, and he was at the vanguard of Dhu al-Qarnayn the Great." al-Naqqash related many reports indicating his longevity, none of which constitutes a proof, as Ibn 'Atiyyah said.

(3) Ibn Abi Hatim related from Qatadah, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: Allah gave Luqman the choice between wisdom and prophethood. He chose wisdom over prophethood. Then Jibril, peace be upon him, came to him while he was asleep, and scattered wisdom over him, so he woke up speaking it. He was asked: "How did you choose wisdom over prophethood, when your Lord gave you the choice?" He said: "If He had sent me prophethood as a binding command, I would have hoped for help from Him in it, and I would have hoped to be able to carry it out. But He gave me the choice, so I feared that I would be too weak for prophethood, so wisdom was dearer to me." al-Suyuti cited it in al-Durr al-Manthur (6/511) and al-Qurtubi in his tafsir (7/5317).

(4) From Abu al-Darda', that he mentioned Luqman the wise and said: He was not given what he was given because of family, nor wealth, nor lineage, nor qualities. But he was a man who was ṣamṣāmah (firm, hard, and solid in character), silent, of long reflection and deep insight. He never slept during the day, and no one ever saw him spit, clear his throat, urinate, defecate, bathe, play, or laugh. He never repeated a statement he had uttered, unless it was a wise saying that he wished to restate. [Al-Suyuti attributed it in al-Durr al-Manthur (6/512) to Ibn Abi Hatim.]

(5) Among the reports related about Luqman the wise is that he said to a man who was looking at him: "If you see me as thick-lipped, then from between them comes gentle speech. And if you see me as black, then my heart is white." [Tafsir al-Qurtubi 7/5317.]

(6) Related by al-Imam Muslim in his Sahih (2564), Ahmad in his Musnad (2/285, 539), and Ibn Majah in his Sunan (4143); the wording is Muslim's.

(7) Related by al-Imam Ahmad in his Musnad (5/411), from Abu Nadrah, from a man among the companions of the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace. Abu Nu'aym related it in Hilyat al-Awliya' (3/100) from Abu Nadrah, from Jabir ibn 'Abd Allah, who said: The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, addressed us in the middle of the days of tashriq, saying: "O people, indeed your Lord is one, and indeed your father is one. Indeed, there is no virtue for an Arab over a non-Arab, nor for a non-Arab over an Arab, nor for a red over a black, nor for a black over a red, except by piety."

(8) He is 'Umar ibn 'Abd al-'Aziz ibn Marwan al-Umawi, Abu Hafs. He was born in Medina in the year 61 AH and grew up there. He was appointed governor of Medina by al-Walid, then Sulayman ibn 'Abd al-Malik made him his vizier in Syria. He became caliph by Sulayman's appointment in the year 99 AH, and was given the oath of allegiance in the mosque of Damascus. He prohibited the cursing of 'Ali ibn Abi Talib, which the Umayyads before him had practiced from the pulpits. He died at the age of about forty in the year 101 AH, and his caliphate lasted two and a half years.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 31, verse 13:

Then the Truthful, Glorified is He, says:

﴿And when Luqman said to his son, while he was instructing him: "O my son, do not associate others with Allah. Indeed, association [with Him] is a tremendous wrong."﴾ (31:13)

God, Glorified is He, gives us a portion of the wisdom of Luqman that the Noble Qur'an has related: ﴿And when Luqman said to his son, while he was instructing him...﴾ (31:13) His saying: ﴿And when...﴾ (31:13), i.e., remember, O Muhammad, when Luqman said to his son. The guidance of Luqman's wisdom and his advice to his son shows us the truth of what is narrated about him: that he used to give legal opinions (fatwa) to people and admonish them before our master Dawud, peace be upon him. When Dawud came, Luqman refrained and said: "Shall I not be content, when I have been relieved [of the duty]?" Then he directed his advice to one he loves, his child.

For this reason, when the judge Ibn Abi Layla(1) complained to the caliph about Imam Abu Hanifa, may Allah be pleased with him, that he refuted his rulings and judgments, the caliph sent word to him to stop giving legal opinions. While he was at home, his daughter came to him and said: "O my father, such-and-such has happened to me; do you want to ask him (for a ruling)?" What did he say to her, though she was his daughter? He said: "Ask your brother Hammad, for the Commander of the Faithful has forbidden me from giving legal opinions."

There is a difference between a person speaking with the general mass of creation and speaking with his child. The son is the only human in existence whose father wishes that he be better and in a finer condition than himself, and wishes to compensate in his son for what he missed in himself and to make up in him for the good he failed to attain.

The meaning of ﴿and he was instructing him...﴾ (31:13) is admonition (wa'z): it is reminding someone of a matter they already knew, for fear that they might forget it. Admonition is not with new information; rather it alerts your heedlessness to something present with you that you have neglected. There is a difference between a scholar who knows and an admonisher who admonishes. The admonition to the son means that he too was knowledgeable in the matters, and the father's role was to advise and remind him.

We notice in the style of the verse that when Allah related it, He said: ﴿And when Luqman said to his son...﴾ (31:13), and when Luqman spoke about his son he said: ﴿O my son...﴾ (31:13), and did not say "O my son" in the form "ibni." This diminutive is a diminutive of tenderness and affection, and it suggests to him: you still need my advice, and beware of thinking that you have grown up and married and so have become independent of me.

The first admonition of a father to a son is: ﴿Do not associate others with Allah...﴾ (31:13). This is the summit of beliefs, and therefore he began with it, because he wants to correct his understanding of existence and draw his attention to the fact that the things by which your fathers and grandfathers were blessed still give forth in the universe. Remarkably, they remain, while the beneficiary who benefited from them dies, and they continue to be given.

Consider: since Allah created the universe, how many generations of mankind have benefited from the sun? Yet they have all perished, while the sun still remains. Likewise the moon, the air, the mountains, and so on. How, then, when you are the master of this universe, should its servant be longer-lived than you?

So the intelligent person must reflect, and the human being whom Allah has honored above the rest of creation must say: "There must be a lifespan for me longer than the lifespan of these creatures that serve me." This is not achieved except when your life in this world is joined to your life in the Hereafter, and this requires that you believe in Allah and not associate anything with Him, for He alone, Glorified is He, created all of this for you and prepared it for your service before you existed.

And recite: ﴿This is the creation of Allah, so show me what those other than Him have created...﴾ (31:11).

How, then, do you claim that Allah has partners in creation, when they themselves have not claimed that they are gods or that they created anything in the universe of Allah? How, when you walk in the desert and see a stone that pleases you, you take it, shape it, and make it a god, and if the wind blew it would knock it over?

Then, what method have these gods brought you? What have they commanded you and what have they forbidden you? What bliss have they prepared for whoever worships them, and what punishment have they prepared for whoever disbelieves in them? So these are gods without obligation, and worship in its reality is that the worshipper obeys the command of the one worshipped. Thus they are false gods whose falsehood is not hidden from the intelligent.

Therefore Luqman says: ﴿Indeed, association [with Him] is a tremendous wrong.﴾ (31:13) Yes, association is wrong, because wrong means: transferring the right of another to another. The summit and ultimate of wrong is that you take the right of Allah and give it to other than Allah. Do you not see that the Companions were troubled when the saying of the Exalted was revealed: (2) ﴿Those who believe and do not mix their belief with wrong—those will have security, and they are guided.﴾ (6:82)

They said: "O Messenger of Allah, which of us has not mixed his belief with wrong?" The Messenger of Allah calmed their fear and reassured them, because the wrong meant here is the greatest wrong, namely associating others with Allah: ﴿Indeed, association [with Him] is a tremendous wrong.﴾ (31:13)

1 He is Muhammad ibn Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Layla al-Ansari al-Kufi: a judge and jurist, one of the people of opinion (ahl al-ra'y). Born in 74 AH. He held the judgeship and rule in Kufa for the Umayyads and then for the Abbasids, and remained in office for 33 years. He has reports with Imam Abu Hanifa and others. He died in Kufa in the year 148 AH at the age of 75 (al-A'lam of al-Zirikli 6/189; Tadhkirat al-Huffaz of al-Dhahabi 1/171).

2 From Abdullah ibn Mas'ud, who said: When this verse ﴿Those who believe and do not mix their belief with wrong... (6:82)﴾ was revealed, it weighed heavily on the people, and they said: "O Messenger of Allah, which of us has not wronged himself?" He said: "It is not what you mean. Have you not heard the righteous servant's words: ﴿Indeed, association [with Him] is a tremendous wrong (31:13)﴾? It is only association." A hadith agreed upon, related by al-Bukhari in his Sahih (4776), and likewise Muslim in his Sahih (142), Book of Faith.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 31, verse 14:

Then the Truthful, glorified is He, says:

﴿We enjoined upon man (kindness) to his parents: his mother carried him in weakness upon weakness, and his weaning is in two years, [saying]: Give thanks to Me and to your parents; to Me is the final return.(14)﴾.

Is this one of the admonitions of Luqman to his son, or is it a new statement from God, the Exalted, that came in the context of Luqman's words? They said: it is from the speech of the Truthful, blessed and exalted is He, as evidenced by His saying after it: ﴿And if they strive with you to make you associate with Me that of which you have no knowledge, do not obey them...(15)﴾ [Luqman].

It is among the honours of Luqman that God related this admonition after his admonition to his son, so it came as if it were a report about him.

The meaning of ﴿We enjoined... (14)﴾ [Luqman] is: We taught and admonished. Both indicate information that begins with what We taught and is recalled in Our admonition, and is fulfilled when We gathered all good in one word. Therefore, when the Prophet (ﷺ) addressed the people in the Farewell Pilgrimage, he mentioned the foremost virtues. Why? Because it was his last speech to them, and the occasion does not suit mentioning all the details of the religion. So he sufficed with mentioning its foundations and principles, like a man among us when death approaches him, who gathers his children and advises them, choosing the important matters and the essence within the narrowest scope.

God, the Exalted, says: ﴿We enjoined upon man to his parents... (14)﴾ [Luqman]. The enjoining of kindness to parents in particular has taken a wide scope in the Book of God. In this verse, the reason for the enjoining is mentioned, so He said: ﴿his mother carried him in weakness upon weakness, and his weaning is in two years... (14)﴾ [Luqman].

In five other verses the word (ihsanan, kindness) occurs, in His saying: ﴿And when We took the covenant of the Children of Israel: You shall not worship except God, and (show) kindness to parents...(83)﴾ [al-Baqarah].

In Surat al-Nisa: ﴿Worship God and do not associate anything with Him, and (show) kindness to parents...(36)﴾ [al-Nisa].

In al-An'am: ﴿Say: Come, I will recite what your Lord has forbidden you: that you associate nothing with Him, and (show) kindness to parents...(151)﴾ [al-An'am].

In al-Isra: ﴿And your Lord has decreed that you worship none but Him, and (show) kindness to parents...(23)﴾ [al-Isra].

In al-Ahqaf: ﴿And We have enjoined upon man kindness to his parents. His mother carried him with hardship and gave birth to him with hardship, and his carrying and weaning are thirty months...(15)﴾ [al-Ahqaf].

In one verse only the word (husnan, goodness) occurs, in Surat al-Ankabut: ﴿And We have enjoined upon man goodness to his parents...(8)﴾ [al-Ankabut].

And in one verse also, the enjoining of parents came without mention of these two words (husnan and ihsanan), and it is the verse we are discussing.

But what is the difference between (ihsanan) and (husnan)? The difference is that ihsan is the verbal noun of ahsana, and ahsana is an event; you say: so-and-so did kindness (ahsana ihsanan). As for husnan, it derives from husn, which is the original source of this root, as you say: so-and-so is just (adil), so you describe him with justice; if you want to exaggerate this description, you say: so-and-so is justice (adl), meaning in his very essence, not merely a description of him.

Thus: husnan is more emphatic in description than ihsanan. So why did it come in this verse in particular: ﴿We enjoined upon man goodness to his parents (8)﴾ [al-Ankabut]? They said: because this verse deals with a difficult matter that touches the summit of belief, for the two parents will ask the son to associate partners with God.

Therefore the matter required that we enjoin the son with goodness in its essence and in its highest emphasis, so it did not say here (ihsanan) but said (husnan), lest he think that their call to him to polytheism justifies insulting them or abandoning them. Thus our Lord teaches us: ﴿do not obey them, but keep them company in this world honourably (15)﴾ [Luqman].

And although the enjoining here is of parents, the grounds of the enjoining are specific to the mother: ﴿his mother carried him in weakness upon weakness, and his weaning is in two years (14)﴾ [Luqman]. He did not mention anything about the role of the father. Why? They said: because the speech here is the speech of a Lord, and you have only to apply your mind and heart to it to reach its subtleties.

God, the Exalted, reminds us here of the role of the mother in particular, because she makes for you while you are small and do not perceive her making; it is hidden from you and you do not know it. As for the actions and making of the father for you, they came in your adulthood and your perception of the affairs around you, so the son knows what his father offered for his sake.

It is as if the father's actions appeared when the conscious mental age was formed, so the son understood what his father did. He often heard: your father went to such-and-such, your father brought you such-and-such, and this matter when your father comes... etc. So the role of the father is apparent, unlike the role of the mother; therefore the Truthful, blessed and exalted, mentioned it here: ﴿his mother carried him in weakness upon weakness (14)﴾ [Luqman].

Someone may say: is the son not the result of the union of father and mother, so they are equal in it? We say: yes, but the mother's hardship in it is more evident during pregnancy and at birth. Were it not that God tied offspring to desire, people would have renounced it, because of the hardships the mother bears and the consequences of children that the father bears.

We know the story of the woman who went to sue her husband because he wanted to take her son from her. He said to the judge: is the child not your child both together? She said: yes, but he carried him lightly and placed him in desire, and I carried him in weakness upon weakness. So the judge ruled in her favour.

The meaning of ﴿weakness upon weakness... (14)﴾ [Luqman] is: weakness upon weakness. The woman in herself is weak, so her inherent weakness combines with weakness caused by the foetus that feeds from her and grows in her womb day after day. Therefore we have said: among God's wisdom in creating the womb is that He made it capable of stretching and expansion, to contain the foetus through its various stages of pregnancy, until the foetus grows to a degree the womb's expansion cannot bear, so it bursts, announcing the birth of a new human being and another creation, as God said: ﴿Then We produced him as another creation. So blessed is God, the best of creators (14)﴾ [al-Mu'minun].

The foetus was a creation dependent on its mother for its nourishment, breathing and movement, but when God's command came and He permitted its birth, He produced another creation with its own independent life-sustaining components, not connected to its mother.

They call this process (the qarn tash), as a balloon bursts when it is inflated beyond what it can bear. Remarkably, the womb expands by God's power to hold several twins, as we see and hear.

Among the greatness of the Creator, glorified is He, in the matter of provision is that the foetus's provision comes to it separated from its mother's provision; each of them has a provision that the other does not take. It is known that when a woman is destined to conceive, the blood that used to flow periodically when the womb was empty of pregnancy stops; this blood is what God made nourishment for the new foetus.

But if pregnancy is not decreed for her, her body expels this blood and rids itself of it without benefiting from it. Why? Because it is not her nourishment. It is as if the Creator, mighty and majestic, is alerting us that each of us has his provision which does not pass to another.

Also, among His wisdom, may He be exalted, in placing the foetus in its mother's womb is that at birth it descends head-first, and this is the natural position for the birth of a healthy child, because the first necessity of life for the child at the moment it separates from its mother is to breathe. If it descends head-first, and this is the position doctors try to verify, it is able to breathe even if the descent of the rest of its body is difficult. But if the child descends in the opposite position, it suffocates and dies before its descent is complete.

Then He, glorified is He, says: ﴿and his weaning is in two years (14)﴾ [Luqman]. Weaning (fisal) means separation from the mother regarding breastfeeding. From it comes the name given to the young camel that has become independent of its milk: (fasil), meaning one that has been separated from its mother and has become able to eat and live without her help. Even the weaning of a child from its mother involves hardship and pain for the mother.

As for the sexual act that produced the child, it was a partnership between them. So we must acknowledge that the mother has the greatest role and bears the greatest burden in the matter of children. Therefore she had the greater share in the Prophet's (ﷺ) advice to the Companion who asked him: Who among people is most deserving of my good companionship, O Messenger of God? He (ﷺ) said: Your mother, then your mother, then your mother, then your father, giving each of them according to what he offered.

This matter of weaning is explained in other verses. In Surat al-Baqarah: ﴿The mothers suckle their children for two complete years, for whoever wishes to complete the nursing (233)﴾ [al-Baqarah]. This confirms ﴿and his weaning is in two years (14)﴾ [Luqman].

In another verse which combines pregnancy and nursing: ﴿and his carrying and weaning are thirty months (15)﴾ [al-Ahqaf]. When two years are subtracted from thirty months, the remainder is six months, which is the minimum period of pregnancy.

This matter was relied upon by Imam Ali (may Allah be pleased with him) when he saw Umar (may Allah be pleased with him) wanting to impose the prescribed punishment on a woman who had given birth after six months, because he believed the period of pregnancy is nine months. Ali said to Umar: O Commander of the Faithful, God says otherwise. He said: And what does God say? Ali cited the two verses mentioned above.

﴿and his carrying and weaning are thirty months (15)﴾ [al-Ahqaf].

And the other: ﴿and his weaning is in two years, [saying]: Give thanks to Me and to your parents; to Me is the final return (14)﴾ [Luqman].

Then Ali explained to him that the minimum period of pregnancy, based on these two verses, is six months. Umar said: What an evil situation, to be in a land where Abu al-Hasan is not present.

As for His saying: ﴿Give thanks to Me and to your parents; to Me is the final return (14)﴾ [Luqman], God, the Exalted, is the one deserving of gratitude first, because He is the one who originated from nothing and sustained from nothing. Then the parents, because they are the cause of the bringing into existence and the production of the child.

It is as if the Truthful, glorified is He, is the highest Causer, because He created from nothing, and the parents are among the means of God in existence. Therefore, do not perfect your gratitude to God, the first Creator and highest Causer, until you perfect gratitude to your parents, who are your second cause of existence.

So His saying, glorified is He: ﴿Give thanks to Me and to your parents; to Me is the final return (14)﴾ [Luqman] means: for bringing into existence. But in another place: ﴿And say: My Lord, have mercy on them as they raised me when I was small (24)﴾ [al-Isra]. This is for bringing into existence, for upbringing, and for care. Just as there is a fatherhood of origination, there is a fatherhood of upbringing. We often find a child raised by someone other than his father and mother, and these must have a share of gratitude, loyalty and kindness, since God the Exalted mentioned them in the cause: ﴿And say: My Lord, have mercy on them as they raised me when I was small (24)﴾ [al-Isra].

The effective cause revolves with its effect in existence and non-existence. If the true father has no existence, then fatherhood belongs to the one who raised him, and he has the same rights as a father regarding gratitude, kindness and affection. Indeed his right should be doubled, because in the true father there is the affection of flesh for flesh, and in the adoptive father there is the affection of religion for religion. This is a matter distinct from mere fatherhood.

But, is God's being thanked first a training for you to thank your parents, who are the direct cause of your existence? Or is thanking your parents a training for you to thank God, who created and brought you into existence? We say: both together. Thanking God entails thanking the parents, and thanking the parents leads to thanking God.

His saying: ﴿to Me is the final return (14)﴾ [Luqman] means: the place of return. The meaning is: I enjoin upon you the most important thing, so beware of opposing my command, for I am able to punish whoever opposes.

1 It is said: this is among what Luqman enjoined upon his son, which God related about him; that is, Luqman said to his son: Do not associate partners with God, and do not obey your parents in associating partners, for God enjoined them to be obeyed in matters that are not polytheism or disobedience to God, the Exalted.
It is also said: And when Luqman said to his son: Do not associate partners [with God], and We enjoined upon man goodness to his parents, and We commanded people with this, and Luqman commanded his son with it.
Al-Qurtubi said in his tafsir (7/5320): "Al-Qushayri mentioned these sayings. The correct view is that these two verses were revealed concerning Sa'd ibn Abi Waqqas," according to the majority of the exegetes.
2 That is because the Messenger of God (ﷺ) said in the sermon of this Pilgrimage: "O people, your blood and your property are sacred to you until you meet your Lord, like the sanctity of this day of yours and this month of yours. You will meet your Lord, and He will ask you about your deeds. I have conveyed. Whoever has a trust, let him return it to the one who entrusted him with it. Every usury is abolished, but you have your capital, you do not wrong and you are not wronged..." The full sermon was recorded by Ibn Hisham in al-Sira al-Nabawiyya (4/603, 604).
3 A hadith agreed upon. Recorded by al-Bukhari in his Sahih (5971), and likewise Muslim in his Sahih (2548), Book of Righteousness and Kinship, from the hadith of Abu Hurayra who said: "A man came to the Messenger of God (ﷺ) and said: O Messenger of God, who is most deserving of my good companionship? He said: Your mother. He said: Then who? He said: Your mother. He said: Then who? He said: Your mother. He said: Then who? He said: Then your father."
4 Ibn Kathir said in his tafsir (4/157): "Ali (may Allah be pleased with him) derived from this verse ﴿and his carrying and weaning are thirty months (15)﴾ [al-Ahqaf] together with the one in Luqman ﴿and his weaning is in two years (14)﴾ [Luqman], that the minimum period of pregnancy is six months. It is a strong and correct deduction, and Uthman and a group of the Companions agreed with it."
5 Al-Hakim recorded in his Mustadrak (1/457), and al-Bayhaqi in Shu'ab al-Iman, from Abu Sa'id al-Khudri who said: "We performed Hajj with Umar (may Allah be pleased with him). When he entered the circumambulation, he faced the Black Stone and said: I know that you are a stone that neither harms nor benefits." It is a long hadith, in which Umar (may Allah be pleased with him) said: "I seek refuge in God, the Exalted, from living among a people in whom you are not present, O Abu al-Hasan," after Ali had said to him: "Rather, it does harm and benefit! Does it not testify on the Day of Resurrection for whoever touched it?"

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 31, verse 15:

Then the Almighty says:

﴿But if they strive with you to make you associate with Me that of which you have no knowledge, do not obey them; and keep them company in this world with kindness, and follow the way of those who turn back to Me. Then to Me is your return, and I will inform you of what you used to do.﴾

The Almighty emphasises the matter of parents, as though He, glory be to Him, is supplementing what needs no supplement, for no one may add to what God has said. It is as if someone was disputing with the Messenger of God (ﷺ) concerning the matter of the parents and what was revealed about them, and asked: "What if they order me to disbelieve; should I disbelieve out of obedience to them?" Therefore the ruling from God came concerning this question.

In the verse of al-Ankabut: ﴿And We have enjoined upon man goodness to his parents. But if they strive with you to make you associate with Me that of which you have no knowledge, do not obey them. To Me is your return, and I will inform you of what you used to do.﴾ [al-Ankabut]

There it mentions (hasanan, "goodness") and does not say ﴿and keep them company in this world with kindness...﴾ [Luqman]. It is as if the word hasan (goodness), which is the comprehensive descriptor of all the meanings of goodness, sufficed in place of "keeping company with kindness."

As for the meaning of ﴿jahadaka...﴾ [Luqman]: we say jahada and jahada (with the doubled-root form), where jahada means "exerted himself" (intransitive in its own self), whereas jaahada contains the sense of mufa'alah (reciprocal action) with another. One says: "Fulan jaahada Fulanan," like qaatala (fought). It indicates participation in the act, as if you said: "Amr shaaraka Zayd" (Amr partnered with Zayd): each of them is an agent and each is an object, but agency predominates in one and objecthood in the other.

Thus the meaning of ﴿and if they strive with you...﴾ [Luqman] does not mean a mere word offered in passing, in which they ask you to associate partners with God. Rather, effort and attempts have come from them to draw you into going along with them in associating partners with God. If that happens from them, then my counsel to you is ﴿do not obey them...﴾ [Luqman].

Then beware lest you take their disbelief and their call to you to disbelieve as a cause for enmity towards them, or for severing kinship. Even in disbelief they have a right over you: ﴿and keep them company in this world with kindness...﴾ [Luqman]. Moreover, they disbelieved in Me, and it is I who enjoin you to treat them with kindness.

As for His, the Exalted's, saying: ﴿and follow the way of those who turn back to Me...﴾ [Luqman], it means: you will not be alone; rather, people before you have preceded you, who repented and turned back, so be with them. ﴿Then to Me is your return...﴾ [Luqman], meaning: your refuge is all together.

It is said that this verse was revealed concerning Sa'd ibn Abi Waqqas, of whom the Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "My maternal uncle Sa'd; let a man show me his maternal uncle." When Sa'd embraced Islam, his mother became angry, and she loved him intensely, so she nearly lost her mind. She swore she would not eat, drink, or bathe, and that she would sit exposed in the heat of the sun until he gave up his religion. When Sa'd learned of this, he said: "Leave her. By God, if hunger gnawed at her she would eat; if thirst gnawed at her she would drink; if lice troubled her she would bathe. As for me, I will not turn aside from the religion I am upon." Then ﴿but if they strive with you...﴾ [Luqman] was revealed.

Were one who disbelieves in God and wants those of the believers, such as a son or others, to disbelieve with him, to see God's charge concerning him despite his disbelief, he would know that God, the Exalted, is a merciful Lord who does not deserve this denial from him.

We have already mentioned the sacred hadith in which the earth said: "My Lord, permit me to swallow the son of Adam, for he has eaten of Your provision and withheld Your gratitude." And the heaven said: "My Lord, permit me to drop fragments upon the son of Adam, for he has eaten of Your provision and withheld Your gratitude." And the seas said: "O Lord, permit me to drown the son of Adam, for he has eaten of Your provision and withheld Your gratitude..." etc. Then the Blessed and Exalted Lord said: "Had you created them, you would have shown them mercy."

That is because they are the servants of God and His handiwork. Have you ever seen a craftsman destroy his own craft? It has also come in the prophetic hadith: "God is more delighted at the repentance of His servant than any one of you who lost his mount in a barren desert..."

So: what an excellent Lord He is.

It is related that our master Abraham, peace be upon him, had a guest who appeared to him, and Abraham saw that his bearing was not the bearing of believers. He asked him about his religion, and the man said: "I am one of the worshippers of fire." So Abraham shut the door in his face, and the man departed. God then rebuked His prophet Abraham concerning this man, saying: "O Abraham, do you want to turn him away from his religion for the hospitality of one night, when He has sustained him all his life, while he disbelieves in Me?"

Abraham hastened after the man until he caught up with him, and informed him of God's rebuke to him. The man said: "Indeed, what an excellent Lord, a Lord who rebukes His beloved on account of His enemies!" Then he bore witness that there is no god but God.

So if the disbeliever who wants others to disbelieve knew that God enjoins kindness toward him while he is a disbeliever, and softens hearts toward him, he would return to the courts of faith in God. Therefore we often meet adherents of other religions who love Islam and choose it, and their families become angry with them. We say to one of them: "Be kinder to them in your new religion than you were in your old religion, so that they may know the excellence of your religion. Multiply your goodness and your kindness to them, perhaps that will soften their hearts and incline them toward your religion."

Consider the grandeur of the expression in ﴿and keep them company in this world with kindness...﴾ [Luqman]. He did not say, for example, "give them kindness," but made kindness a companionship that requires following their needs and attending to their affairs, such that the son knows his parents' needs and gives to them before they ask, so that they are not driven to the humiliation of asking. This in itself is another kindness.

Like the man whose friend knocked on his door; when he opened it, the friend confided something to him, and the man went in and gave his friend what he asked for, then entered his house weeping. His wife asked him: "Why are you weeping, when you have given him what he wanted?" He said: "I am weeping because I did not attend to his condition so that I could give him before he humbled himself by asking."

When the Blessed and Exalted Lord says, after the injunction concerning parents: ﴿Then to Me is your return, and I will inform you of what you used to do﴾ [Luqman], He is only alerting us that kindness to parents and keeping them company with kindness will not be forgotten for you; rather, it will be recorded for you and will be in your scales, because you obeyed My command and charge and fulfilled it. So you will be rewarded, because you performed an act of faith for which you must be recompensed.

1 Occasion of revelation of the verse: Sa'd ibn Abi Waqqas said: This verse ﴿But if they strive with you to make you associate with Me that of which you have no knowledge, do not obey them; and keep them company in this world with kindness...﴾ [Luqman] was revealed concerning me. I was a man dutiful to my mother. When I embraced Islam she said: "O Sa'd, what is this new thing I see you have introduced? Either you abandon this religion of yours or I will not eat or drink until I die, and you will be reproached for me, and it will be said: 'O slayer of his mother!'" I said: "O mother, do not do that, for I will not abandon this religion of mine for anything." She remained one day and a night without eating, and in the morning she had become exhausted; she remained another day and night, and her exhaustion had grown severe. When I saw that, I said: "O mother, you know that by God, even if you had a hundred souls and they departed one by one, I would not abandon this religion of mine for anything. So if you wish, eat, and if you wish, do not eat." When she saw that, she ate, and this verse was revealed. Cited by al-Suyuti in al-Durr al-Manthur (6/521), attributing it to Abu Ya'la, al-Tabarani, Ibn Mardawayh and Ibn 'Asakir, from Abu 'Uthman al-Nahdi.

2 Mentioned by Ibn Hajar al-Asqalani in al-Isabah (biography no. 3187), attributing it to al-Tirmidhi from the hadith of Jabir, who said: Sa'd came, and the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "This is my maternal uncle; let a man show me his maternal uncle." It was also related by al-Hakim in his Mustadrak (3/498), who said: sahih according to the conditions of the two Shaykhs, though they did not record it, and by Ibn Sa'd in al-Tabaqat (3/128).

3 She was Hamna bint Sufyan ibn Umayya. Ibn Hajar al-Asqalani said in al-Isabah fi Tamyiz al-Sahabah (biography no. 3187), in the biography of her son Sa'd: "She was the daughter of the paternal uncle of Abu Sufyan ibn Harb ibn Umayya."

4 Cited by Imam al-Ghazali in Ihya' 'Ulum al-Din (4/52) as the saying of some of the early generations, its wording: "No servant disobeys except that the place of his earth asks permission to swallow him, and his ceiling from the sky asks permission to drop fragments upon him. God the Exalted says to the earth and the sky: 'Withhold from My servant and give him respite, for you did not create him. Had you created him, you would have shown him mercy. Perhaps he will repent to Me and I will forgive him, and perhaps he will exchange (his deeds) for righteousness and I will replace them with good deeds for him.'"

5 A hadith agreed upon (Muttafaq 'alayh). Related by al-Bukhari in his Sahih (6309) and likewise Muslim in his Sahih (2747) from the hadith of Anas ibn Malik (may God be pleased with him). In the wording of Muslim: "God is more joyful at the repentance of His servant when he turns to Him than any one of you who was on his mount in a barren desert, and it ran off from him carrying his food and drink, and he despaired of it. Then he came to a tree and lay down in its shade, having despaired of his mount. While he was in that state, behold, it was standing right beside him; he seized its halter and then said, from the intensity of his joy: 'O God, You are my servant and I am Your lord!' He erred out of the intensity of his joy."

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1–53, fragments of 54–66) on surah 31, verse 16:

﴿O my son...﴾ [Luqman] This is also a address of tenderness and affection. ﴿Indeed, it, if it be the weight of a grain of mustard seed...﴾ [Luqman] Luqman wants to point his son to one of the attributes of Almighty God, the attribute of absolute knowledge, from which nothing is hidden,

as if he were saying to him: Beware lest you think that what is hidden from people is hidden from God Most High. ﴿Does not He who created know? And He is the Subtle, the Acquainted.﴾ [al-Mulk]

Just as nothing is hidden from God Most High, not even the weight of a grain of mustard seed, even if it is within a rock, or in the heavens, or in the earth, so too no good deed or evil deed is hidden from Him, however small it is, and however much its doer tries to conceal it.

We have said that the orientalists stopped at the question of God's knowledge of the hidden secrets of His creation, and at His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿He knows what is spoken aloud and He knows what you conceal﴾ [al-Anbiya' 110]. They say: God boasts of knowing what we conceal; how then does He boast of knowing what is spoken aloud, which is known to everyone?

We say: God, glorified is He, in His saying ﴿Indeed, He knows what is spoken aloud and He knows what you conceal﴾ [al-Anbiya' 110] does not address an individual, but addresses a group. He knows the loud speech of a group at one time. We illustrate this with a demonstration, for example, in which thousands of people chant in different voices and various slogans, some of which the law punishes. Can you, with the mixing and overlapping of voices, distinguish between them and trace each word back to its speaker?

You cannot, even though this is loud speech that everyone hears. As for the Truth, blessed and exalted is He, He knows every word, knows who uttered it, and returns every utterance to its speaker. Therefore, it is His right, exalted is He, to boast of knowing what is spoken aloud; indeed, knowledge of what is spoken aloud is greater and more eloquent than knowledge of what is secret.

His saying, exalted is He, ﴿the weight of a grain of mustard seed...﴾ [Luqman 16] means the weight of a mustard seed, which was the smallest thing at that time, so they made it a unit of measure for smallness. It is not for you now to say: Is the mustard seed the smallest thing in existence? The Qur'an mentioned it as an example of smallness according to the people's knowledge of things at the time of its revelation. As for verification, the Qur'an has mentioned the atom (dharrah) and what is smaller than it.

Therefore, when they invented in Germany the device for splitting the indivisible atom (i.e., the part that cannot be divided) and were able to break the atom, they thought that this process was an objection to the Qur'an, since the Qur'an mentioned the atom and made it a religious measure in His saying, exalted is He: ﴿So whoever does an atom's weight of good will see it. And whoever does an atom's weight of evil will see it.﴾ [al-Zalzalah 7–8] But it did not mention what is smaller than it, and it is known that a part is smaller than its whole.

We say: You have read something, and other things escaped you. If you had a grasp of the words of God, you would know that in it there is a precaution against what you have reached and what you will reach later. Read, if you wish, the saying of God about the atom: ﴿Nor is there anything smaller than that or greater, but that it is in a clear register﴾ [Yunus 61].

Rather, we say: the precaution here is a compound precaution, for He did not say "small" but said "smaller" (aṣghar), and this indicates that there is a record in the word of God for every fragment of the atom.

His saying: ﴿...if it were within a rock or in the heavens or in the earth, Allah will bring it forth...﴾ [Luqman 16] "Within a rock" means: in the firm fabric of existence, and in the narrowest place. "Or in the heavens or in the earth" means: in the vast expanse that has no limits. So, neither in the tight, sealed place nor in the expanse is anything hidden from God. ﴿Allah will bring it forth﴾ [Luqman 16]. And accompany the modes of bringing it forth with two attributes of God: ﴿Indeed, Allah is Subtle and Acquainted﴾ [Luqman 16].

He combined these two attributes, because you may have knowledge of a thing and know its place, but you cannot reach it, such as when it is in a narrow place your hand cannot enter, and then you seek help from a precise instrument, such as tweezers for example. The knowledge is present, but you lack subtlety in entering.

The Truth, glorified and exalted is He, is Subtle; however small things are and however fine, He reaches them. Therefore He is Knowing and Acquainted with everything, however small, and Able to bring it forth, however fine; for He is Subtle, and no obstacle can prevent Him. This attribute of subtlety is for penetrating into things.

We know that the finer and more subtle a thing is, the more harmful it can be, even among harmful creatures. We have previously clarified this matter with the example of one who built a house in the open country and wanted to secure its windows from harmful animals and insects. He placed on the windows a mesh of iron that prevents thieves and large animals. Then he remembered mice and snakes, so he narrowed the iron mesh. Then he remembered flies and mosquitoes, so he needed something narrower and finer. Thus: the more subtle and fine your enemy is, the more dangerous he is, and the more precaution he requires.

So His saying, ﴿Indeed, Allah is Subtle and Acquainted﴾ [Luqman 16], means: knowledge of the place is not lacking to Him, nor is there ease and facility in reaching things.

These were some of Luqman's counsels and admonitions to his son. He has not yet commanded him with any of the obligations, but was keen to alert him: you have believed in God, His method has reached you, and you have listened to it. So obey that method in what to do and what not to do. But before you undertake your Lord's method in your conduct, know that you are dealing with a self-subsisting God, who is not overtaken by drowsiness or sleep, and from whom nothing is absent. So approach the method with this belief.

And beware lest the doubt overcome you that you do not see God, for if you do not see Him, He sees you. Know that your deed is recorded against you, even if it is in a deaf, narrow rock, or in the sky, or in a vast land.

This matter is confirmed by the saying of God in a sacred hadith: "O My servants, if you believe that I do not see you, then the flaw is in your faith; and if you believe that I see you, then why have you made Me the least of those you regard?"

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi (surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66)) on surah 31, verse 17:

After that, Luqman enters into his admonition to his son regarding the domain of obligation (taklif), and says to him:

﴿O my son, establish the prayer, enjoin what is right, forbid what is wrong, and be patient over what befalls you. Indeed, that is of the determination of matters (ʿazm al-umur).﴾ (31:17)

These are four matters, which Luqman began with establishing the prayer (salah). Prayer is the first pillar after one bears witness that there is no god but Allah and that Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah. We know that prayer, because of its importance, was prescribed directly (without intermediary), and because of its importance it was made a constant obligation for the believer that never falls from him under any circumstance. As for the remaining pillars, they may fall from you for one reason or another, such as fasting, zakat and hajj. When these pillars fall from you, there remain with you only the two testimonies and the prayer. For this reason the Prophet (ﷺ) made it the pillar of the religion (ʿimad al-din).

This is why Luqman began with it: ﴿O my son, establish the prayer..﴾ (31:17), because it is a continuous declaration of allegiance to Allah, the Exalted, five times a day and night. When your Lord calls you (Allahu akbar), you should not become preoccupied with a creature to the neglect of the call of the Creator. Otherwise, what is the position of a father, for example, when he calls his son and the son does not answer him? So beware: when your Lord calls you, do not fail to answer.

Then reflect on the call to prayer (adhan), which healthy human nature arrived at and which our master, the Messenger of Allah, approved: Allahu akbar, Allahu akbar, meaning, greater than everything that preoccupies you from it. So beware of excusing yourself from establishing the prayer on account of work in farming, industry or trade.

I once discussed this matter with a surgeon, and he said: "How can I leave a surgical operation for the sake of prayer?" I said to him: "By God, if you were compelled to relieve yourself, would you go or not?" He laughed and said: "I would go." I said: "Then prayer is more deserving [of that]. And do not believe that Allah, the Exalted, imposes an obligation on the servant and then begrudges him the breadth of time for it, as evidenced by the fact that He, the Exalted, takes into account the servant's time, interests and capabilities. In travel, for example, combining (jamʿ) and shortening (qasr) are prescribed for you."

So you can arrange your prayers according to the time available to you, either by combining in advance (jamʿ al-taqdim) or by delaying (jamʿ al-taʾkhir). How much your time is broadened and freed from preoccupation with worship, if you combine Zuhr and ʿAsr by combining in advance, and Maghrib and ʿIsha by delaying to the end of the time of ʿIsha? Or when you combine Zuhr and ʿAsr by delaying, praying them before Maghrib, then pray Maghrib and ʿIsha by combining in advance?

So: the matter has latitude, and no one has an excuse for abandoning prayer specifically. As for those who say in such matters ﴿Allah does not burden a soul beyond its capacity..﴾ (2:286), and that this is not within my capacity, we say to them: you should not make your capacity the judge; rather, obligation (taklif) is what judges capacity. Since your Lord, Mighty and Majestic, has imposed the obligation on you, He has known your capacity and imposed on you according to its measure, as evidenced by the concessions (rukhas) He has legislated for you when worship exceeds capacity.

And He said ﴿establish the prayer..﴾ (31:17), because prayer is the first completion, by consensus, of the method of Allah, and through it a person's faith is completed in himself. We have previously said that there is a difference between the pillars of Islam and the pillars of the Muslim. The pillars of Islam are the five well-known ones; the pillars of the Muslim are those that remain with him and never fall from him under any circumstance, namely the two testimonies and the prayer. Although the Muslim must believe in all of them, in practice he may be relieved of other than prayer and the two testimonies.

Then Luqman clarifies to his son that faith does not stop at responding to these two fundamental pillars; rather, among faith and among the perfection of faith is that you love for your brother what you love for yourself. So he says to him: ﴿and enjoin what is right, and forbid what is wrong..﴾ (31:17). Therefore, after your perfection through establishing the prayer, occupy yourself with enjoining what is right and forbidding what is wrong. Through prayer you are perfected in your own self, and through enjoining good and forbidding evil you transmit that perfection to others, and in that is the perfection of faith.

When you enjoin what is right and when you forbid what is wrong, do not think that you are giving charity to others; rather, you are performing a deed whose benefit returns to you. Through it you find the breadth of ease in faith, and you find tranquility and personal peace, because you have discharged the obligations while others fell short and became remiss.

Without doubt, in the commitment of others and their walking upon the method of Allah there is rest for you too; otherwise, the whole society suffers because of this small group that departs from the method of Allah.

And among the honoring of knowledge is that you do not benefit from it fully unless you transmit it to others. If you conceal it, others benefit from your goodness while you suffer from their evil. So: you do not benefit from the good of others except when you perform this obligation, by enjoining others to what is right and forbidding them from what is wrong, and loving for them what you love for yourself. Thereby you attain both shares: your share with Allah, because you performed it, and your share with people, because you are in a society of complete faith that benefits you and does not harm you.

You may also note that this verse did not link establishing the prayer with giving zakat, as is the usual pattern of the verses. Frequently we read: ﴿And establish the prayer and give zakat..﴾ (2:43).

When we survey the word zakat in the Noble Qur'an, we find it occurs thirty-two times. Two of these are not in the sense of the well-known zakat of wealth, which is general growth, but in the sense of purification, namely in the Lord's saying concerning the story of al-Khidr and Musa, upon them both be peace: ﴿Have you killed a pure soul without [its having killed] another?..(18:74)﴾.

Then His saying: ﴿So we wanted that their Lord should replace them with one better than him in purity (zakat) and nearer in mercy (81)﴾ (Al-Kahf).

The meaning: We purified them when we lifted from them a door of trial in the religion of Allah.

The other occurrence is in His saying: ﴿And affection from Us and purity (zakah)..(19:13)﴾ [Maryam]. The meaning: We granted Maryam something by which to purify her; for zakat is first transferred from one who has to one who lacks, and Maryam had not married, so she was lacking in this respect; therefore Allah granted her special growth from another aspect when He breathed into her of His Spirit, the Exalted.

In one place, zakat came in the sense of zakat of wealth, but not linked with prayer, namely in His saying: ﴿And what you give in usury to increase within the wealth of people will not increase with Allah; but what you give in zakat, desiring the Face of Allah, those are the multipliers (39)﴾ (Al-Rum).

In this verse Luqman said to his son: ﴿O my son, establish the prayer and enjoin what is right..(31:17)﴾, and did not say: "and give zakat." Why?

It should be pointed out that the Qur'an joined prayer and zakat, because prayer involves a sacrifice of time, and time is the occasion of work, and work is the means of earning and wealth. So: when you pray an hour, you have sacrificed the time which is the root of wealth; it is as though in prayer you have given in charity one hundred percent of the wealth earned in that time. As for zakat, you give a tenth, or half a tenth, or a quarter of a tenth, and most of your earnings remain with you. Thus in fact the zakat within prayer is greater and more eloquent than zakat itself.

So: since zakat is in each of them, the Qur'an joined them, except in this place. When you reflect upon it, you find it among the subtleties of Qur'anic style. The Qur'an relates these counsels of Luqman to his son, and for us there are two observations:

The first: Allah did not obligate the servant except after the age of puberty, except in prayer, and He directed this obligation to the father or guardian, delegating to him that he should obligate his son to pray and punish him if he neglects its performance. This is so that the habit of prayer grows in the son, such that when the age of obligation arrives, he has become accustomed to it and familiar with it, for it is a worship that in the beginning needs training and back-and-forth. This is more suitable for the early age.

The father obligates his son on the basis that he is the second originator of him and the direct cause of his existence, as though Allah, the Exalted, says: "I am the originator of you all, and I have delegated to you that you obligate your son, because your favor is manifest to Him, and your bounties upon him are many; you are the one who looks after his interests and fulfills his desires. If you command him, he accepts from you and obeys you, and that obedience is by your price."

And since I have delegated to you the obligation, it is natural that I delegate to you the punishment. If there is negligence in this matter, the violation is from you, not from the son, because I did not obligate him; I obligated you.

Therefore Luqman began his commands to his son with establishing the prayer, because he is charged with this command. His son is still young, as evidenced by his saying ﴿O my son..(31:17)﴾. So the obligation here is from the father. If the son were adult at the time of this command, the meaning would be: take note of the obligation from Allah to establish the prayer.

As for zakat, which is also an obligation from Allah, he did not mention it here; this is from Luqman's wisdom and precision of expression, and the Qur'an related it to us so that we may take from it principles to live by.

Second: if he obligated him with zakat, saying "establish the prayer and give zakat," he would have attributed ownership to his son, and it is well known that a son has no ownership while his father is alive, as evidenced by the saying of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ): "You and your wealth belong to your father."(1) We have mentioned that when Luqman learned of his father's death, he said: "Then I have become master of my own affair."(2) So his affair was not his own while his father lived. Therefore he did not command his son with zakat; zakat is an obligation upon himself, not upon his son.

This matter is confirmed for us when we read the Lord's saying: ﴿There is no blame upon the blind, nor upon the lame, nor upon the sick, nor upon yourselves that you eat from your houses or the houses of your fathers or the houses of your mothers or the houses of your brothers or the houses of your sisters or the houses of your paternal uncles or the houses of your paternal aunts or the houses of your maternal uncles or the houses of your maternal aunts, or that which you possess the keys to, or your friend..(24:61)﴾ [An-Nur].

So Allah removed the blame from us to eat from these houses. We note that the verse mentioned relatives other than children; the logical order would have been to say after "your mothers": "or the houses of your children." Why was the houses of children not mentioned here? They said: because it is included in His saying "your houses": the house of the son is the house of the father, and the son and what his hands possess belong to his father.

Then Luqman says to his son: ﴿and be patient over what befalls you..(31:17)﴾. Patience (sabr) is compelling the soul to endure events, so that events do not aid you against yourself through despair. You, facing events, need doubled strength, so how would you weaken yourself before them?

A misfortune either has an adversary for you in it, or it has no adversary for you. For example, one who falls and his leg breaks, or one who is suddenly struck by illness, etc.: these are decrees that Allah drove toward you without a cause, so there is no adversary for you in them. Therefore He places them in your balance: either they raise your ranks, or they expiate your sins. This is why the disbelievers would rejoice when a misfortune befell the Muslims, as they rejoiced on the day of Uhud. Allah refuted them and made clear their foolishness, and the Exalted said: ﴿Say: Never will we be struck except by what Allah has decreed for us..(9:51)﴾. Reflect on the prepositional phrase "for us" (lana), and He did not say "decreed against us" (alayna). So the misfortune is in the account of "for him" (lahu), not "against him." Why then do you rejoice when a misfortune strikes the Muslims?

He enjoined patience after enjoining what is right and forbidding what is wrong, because whoever is exposed to these two matters will inevitably suffer harm as a result of enjoining good or forbidding evil. If you are exposed to harm, then be patient, for this patience will give you ample reward.

The changing of wrong has stages, which the Prophet (ﷺ) clarified in his saying: "Whoever among you sees an evil, let him change it with his hand; if he cannot, then with his tongue; if he cannot, then with his heart, and that is the weakest of faith."(3)

So Allah commanded you to change wrong, but He left to you the assessment of the matter and the extent of your ability in it. The religion wants you to be a reformer, but it does not want you to throw yourself into destruction. You may change the wrong with your hand, striking and preventing, if you have authority over the wrongdoer, such as your son or your brother, etc.

So you may, for example, strike him if you see a cigarette in his mouth, or break for him the cup of wine if he drinks it, or tear...
