Then the Truth, glorified is He, says:

﴿Your creation and your resurrection are only like that of a single soul. Indeed, Allah is Hearing and Seeing.﴾ (28)

The Truth, glorified and exalted is He, always emphasises the matter of resurrection (al-ba'th) and the Last Day (al-qiyamah), and He wants, glorified is He, to set up for people in the movement of their lives the scales of recompense (mawazin al-jaza'), because every action in which there are no scales of recompense is considered a vain action. Recompense, in the form of reward and punishment, cannot be dispensed with except by one who is infallible (ma'sum) or one who is compelled (musakhkhar). The infallible is constantly engaged in doing good, and the compelled has no choice in whether he acts or does not act.

So, if the principle of recompense, in reward and punishment, is not established apart from these two, corruption must arise. If the one who has free choice is not rewarded for doing and not punished for abandoning, the movement of life becomes disordered. Even in societies that do not believe in a god, they have established for themselves this law, the law of reward and punishment.

The Truth, glorified and exalted is He, gives us an example of this principle in His saying, from the story of Dhu al-Qarnayn:

﴿Indeed, We established him in the land and gave him of every thing a means (sabab).﴾ (84) ﴿So he followed a means.﴾ (85) [al-Kahf]

He, glorified is He, wanted to show that the man established in the land has a mission. This mission is to thank Allah for the establishment (al-tamkin), and this is not achieved except by establishing the scale of justice in the universe. ﴿Until, when he reached the setting-place of the sun...﴾ (86) [al-Kahf], that is, in the apparent view, for it does not set in reality; it sets for one group in one place and rises upon another group in another place.

﴿He found it setting in a spring of black mud, and found near it a people. We said: O Dhu al-Qarnayn, either you punish them or you take among them a good course.﴾ (86) [al-Kahf]

No one is entrusted with the power to punish or to take the good course unless he has standards and the scale of justice. Allah said of him: ﴿And We gave him of every thing a means.﴾ (84) [al-Kahf], that is, a blessing and a measure for distributing this blessing. Allah's blessing upon him was not limited to his being a possessor of authority and dominion; rather, he had the means of life, and he had the scale of justice that regulates the flow of blessings throughout the whole universe.

So the one who was given the choice to act or not to act wanted to show his method: he did not take choice as a means to fix desires. Therefore, after this, He said: ﴿As for him who does wrong, We will punish him; then he will be returned to his Lord, and He will punish him with a terrible punishment.﴾ (87) [al-Kahf] This is the punishment. ﴿And as for him who believes and does righteousness, he will have a good reward, and We will speak to him of Our command with ease.﴾ (88) [al-Kahf], that is, after he attains his reward, We give him beyond that incentives that encourage him, and We hold for him a ceremony of honour so as to entice others to follow his path.

So, the matter of reward and punishment is a necessary affair. If this is so in particular worldly affairs, it is more fitting in matters of religion and values, which control all the scales of life. There must be a time for reward and for punishment; otherwise injustice spreads, it destroys people, and takes from them all the enjoyments of life. The corrupter benefits from that, and whoever adheres to the religion of Allah and the values of His method is ruined.

Therefore you find the Truth, blessed and exalted is He, always emphasising the matter of resurrection, the Last Day and the reckoning, and you see the enemies of religion trying to cast doubt on this matter and to dislodge people from belief in it by various means.

The philosophers have a role in this, the atheists have a role, and the People of the Book have a role. For example, you find that the Torah is almost devoid of any reference to the Last Day, and this is a strange matter that cannot be conceived in a book, a heavenly religion and a way of life.

This is only because the People of the Torah wanted to dislodge people from several matters in order to establish for themselves a temporal, material authority. They even coveted raising this authority until they reached Allah, the Exalted, as the Qur'an relates about them: ﴿And when you said: O Musa, we will not believe you until we see Allah openly...﴾ (55) [al-Baqarah]

When Allah sent down to them the manna, which is a sweet substance like the taste of cream, and made it fall upon them, and sent down to them the quails, which are birds like the quail-like fowl that descend upon them ready prepared for consumption, they rejected Allah's gift to them and His food that was prepared for them, and said: Rather we want food that we make with our hands. And they said: ﴿We will not endure one kind of food...﴾ (61) [al-Baqarah], so He said to them: ﴿Go down to a city, for you will have what you asked for...﴾ (61) [al-Baqarah].

Since the matter for these people is material, they must remove themselves from the Hereafter, from the Resurrection and the reckoning, and therefore they set about casting doubt upon them. As for the philosophers, they said: When Allah resurrects a human being after death, his limbs having decomposed and become dust, and then a tree is planted in this place and is nourished by this dust, and another person eats from its fruits, and some cells and particles of the first are transferred to him, then if there is a resurrection, will these particles be resurrected with the first or with the second? If they are with the first, then this is a deficiency in the second, and vice versa. This is the doubt of the philosophers.

The philosophers have floundered in this confusion because they did not perceive anything in existence that gives values to the unseen. We have clarified this matter and said to them: If a person weighing, for example, one hundred kilos is afflicted with an illness that causes him to lose forty kilos of his weight, what does this loss mean for the person himself?

This matter is governed by two things: nourishment and excretion. In the period of growth, what enters the body is more than what leaves it; in the period of old age, for example, what leaves is more. If the two balance, there is a state of stability in which the person neither gains nor loses, and this is the period of stability.

So, the person who lost forty kilos of weight, then Allah healed him and his health returned, so that his weight increased and returned to its natural state: Did the person change during the loss of his weight? And did he change when he returned to his normal state? Or did his personhood and selfhood remain the same?

So, the matter in the formation of the body is not atoms and particles; rather, it is a special immaterial personality, even if it is formed from particles of matter, namely the sixteen elements that make up the human body, beginning with oxygen and ending with manganese, which are the same elements that make up the soil of the earth from which we eat, and these elements in proportions that differ from one person to another.

The Truth, glorified is He, says: ﴿We know what the earth diminishes of them, and with Us is a preserved record.﴾ (4) [Qaf], meaning: We know what has been lost from each person: so much iron, so much oxygen, so much phosphorus, and so on.

So, when Allah resurrects the human being after death, He resurrects this immaterial personality with these known parts, and the person comes back exactly the same.

Among the issues they have raised concerning resurrection and the confusions they try to create, they say: Allah creates the human being in a period of nine months, or six months, passing during it through several stages: nutfah, then 'alaqah, then mudghah, then bones, then He clothes the bones with flesh. This is for one human being. So how long does the re-creation of mankind take from Adam, peace be upon him, until the Hour arrives?

We say: You have mentioned how the offspring of man is created, which takes nine or six months, but you have not mentioned the creation of the origin, which is Adam, peace be upon him. Allah created him in his form and shape in which he was; he was not small and then grew, rather he was created adult, mature and complete, and then the spirit was breathed into him.

Furthermore, the elements of an action are: the act, the agent, and the one acted upon, to which is added the time in which the action takes place. For I want to move this "load" from here to there: our moving is an act, I am the agent, the load is the one acted upon, then the time the event takes. Time means the distribution of the parts of the event over the parts of time. If you want to sew a garment by hand, it takes you a long time, but if you sew it by machine, it takes far less.

So, the time of an action is proportionate to the strength of the agent. You remember that in the past streets were lit by oil lamps, and each area had a worker who climbed a ladder to each lamp to light it; but now you can light an entire city with the press of one button. So, the more the strength increases, the less the time becomes.

So come now to the matter of resurrection and re-creation after death: is it by your own strength, so that you calculate it according to your strength and capacity? No, it is by the power of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, and Allah does not deal with matters as we do, nor does He labour at them; rather He, glorified is He, acts by "Be" (kun). So, the act with respect to Allah, exalted is He, does not need a time in which the parts of the act are distributed over the parts of time.

Do you not consider this unlikely with regard to Allah, when your Lord has given you a portion of it despite your limited capacity? Do you not sit in such a gathering, seeing all of us at once in a single glance, and likewise hear all of us at one time? Do you not stand up as soon as you wish to stand up, and your limbs move for you as soon as the action occurs to your mind? Do you reflect on the muscles that moved and the signals that took place within you so that you might stand from your seat?

We have already clarified this matter when we compared the movement of a human being, in its smoothness and the obedience of the limbs to the will of their owner, with the movement of an excavator, for example, which performs no movement except by pressing a specific button for it.

So if you, O servant, have your limbs and organs respond to your will regarding things, do you find it unlikely with respect to Allah that He should act by the word "Be"? How, when you yourself act without even saying it; mere will on your part does what you wish.

If you say: How does the Truth, glorified is He, act by the word "Be", when I act without saying it? We say: Yes, you act without "Be", because things are not subject to your command; rather they are made subservient by the first "Be" when Allah said to them "Be" as subservient to His will. So: I act without "Be" because it is not within my power. Thus the first "Be" from Allah, exalted is He, is "Be" for all of us.

By this understanding we have been able to interpret the event of the Night Journey and Ascension, and to refute those who deny it. Allah says: ﴿Glory be to Him who took His servant by night from al-Masjid al-Haram to al-Masjid al-Aqsa...﴾ (1) [al-Isra].

When the disbelievers heard of the event, they denied it and said: How, when we travel to it on the backs of camels for a month? Yes, you travel to it on the backs of camels for a month, because your action requires time and practice, in which the parts of the action are distributed over the parts of time. But Muhammad did not say "I travelled", which would make him in the action like one of you; rather he said: "I was taken by night" (usriya bi).(1)

So it is carried by another power: the action is not ascribed to him but to the one who carries him, to Allah. And we have said: the more the strength increases, the less the time becomes; so when the strength is the strength of the Truth, blessed and exalted is He, there is no time. Therefore He, glorified is He, says regarding creation and re-creation: ﴿Your creation and your resurrection are only like that of a single soul...﴾ (28) [Luqman].

So the matter is easy for Allah, because the creation of a single soul and the creation of all souls is accomplished by "Be", and the matter does not need nine or six months.

We gave an example to clarify this matter with the making of yoghurt, for example: you bring milk, add the known culture, and leave it at a certain temperature, and it turns by itself into the yoghurt you want. Did you sit in front of every jar and transform it yourself, or did you perform the known procedure of this craft and then leave these materials to react by themselves?

Likewise, Allah willed that the human being exist as a foetus in his mother's womb, and that the processes of growth proceed upon him according to their nature. So: the creation of the human being is not measured, with respect to Allah, by time. Imam 'Ali, may Allah ennoble his face, resolved this matter when he was asked: How does Allah reckon all people from Adam, peace be upon him, until the Hour, at one time?

He said: He reckons them all at one time.

(1) A hadith agreed upon (muttafaq 'alayh), related by al-Bukhari in his Sahih (4710), and Muslim in his Sahih (170), from the hadith of Jabir ibn 'Abd Allah, may Allah be pleased with him.

Then the Almighty says:

﴿Have you not seen that Allah causes the night to enter into the day and causes the day to enter into the night, and He has subjected the sun and the moon, each running to a specified term, and that Allah is Acquainted with what you do?﴾ (29)

These are clear cosmic signs, visible to everyone: to the believer and the disbeliever, the obedient and the disobedient. Allah Almighty apportions our time between night and day, but this apportioning is not equal in a mechanical sense, such that each of them is a fixed twenty-four hours by mere arithmetical determination, as people say. For this reason we see that the day falls short of twenty-four hours by several minutes, which are added to the length of the night, or vice versa.

For this reason, in the days of Ptolemy they said: the year is 365 days, five hours, fifty-five minutes and twelve seconds, precisely. Afterwards they arrived at the conclusion that the year is 365 days and a quarter of a day, by way of calculation (jabr), so every three years they compensate the fourth. They say: a common year (sanah basitah) and a leap year (sanah kabisah), that is, a long year. So the year that is divisible by four is a leap year, and for this reason we find that February in this year has 29 days, in order to compensate for the day.

The word "day" means night and day, but the division between them is not equal. Allah, blessed and exalted, in His wise creation, willed to distribute heat and cold over all regions of the inhabited earth, and to give each region what it needs so that its land may bring forth vegetation and provide us with the means of our life. The evidence is that some plants grow only in summer, and some grow only in winter, as well as in the spring equinox and the autumn equinox.

Therefore, we have finally come to know that the Creator, glorified be He, gave the axis of the earth a tilt of about 23.5 degrees from the plane of its orbit, so it is not level. In winter the greater part of it faces the night and the other part faces the day, so you find winter nights longer and colder than summer nights. The winter night reaches its maximum possible length, twelve hours, in the month of Kiyahk, so much so that the farmers say in Kiyahk: "Kiyak, good morning, good evening, get up from your sleep, your dinner is ready."

In contrast, in the summer season, the tilt of the earth's axis is, as it were, one of the secrets of the engineering of this universe. On the twenty-first of June the summer solstice begins, and on the twenty-third of December the winter solstice begins, then the spring equinox on the twenty-first of March, and the autumn equinox on the twenty-second of September. At the spring equinox and the autumn equinox you find that the night is equal to the day, and their climate is temperate, neither hot nor cold.

So the saying of Allah, the Exalted: ﴿Have you not seen that Allah causes the night to enter into the day and causes the day to enter into the night…﴾ (29) means: do not suppose that the night and the day are an equal division, because Allah in His wisdom causes a portion of the night to enter into the day, or a portion of the day to enter into the night, thus increasing one and decreasing the other, for a wisdom He willed, glorified and exalted be He, for the benefit of man and for supplying him with the means of his life, so that you may know that whatever changes occur in the night or the day have their basis in the supreme divine wisdom.

When we divide the day into night and day, which, as we have said, is neither monotonous nor equal, the night has a function in life and the day has a function, as He, glorified be He, has made clear to us: ﴿And We made the night as a covering (10) and We made the day for livelihood﴾ (11) [al-Naba'].

The meaning of "covering" (libas) is that you dwell in it, are concealed, and cover yourself. For this reason we later learned that light during sleep is something unhealthy, and we understood the saying of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ: "Extinguish the lamps when you go to sleep."(1)

The Almighty clarifies this matter for us in His saying: ﴿By the morning brightness (1) and by the night when it covers (2)﴾ [al-Duha], and He says: ﴿By the night when it covers (1) and by the day when it appears in brightness (2)﴾ [al-Layl], to show you that each of them has a function in the movement of your life. The day is for movement and the night is for rest, and you should not confuse these two functions without cause. We have made an exception to this rule for those whose nature of work obliges them to work at night and rest by day.

The Creator, Mighty and Majestic, placed in the movement of night and day secrets and wonders which we should attend to through the data of science. It is part of the wisdom of the Creator, glorified be He, that He made for every secret in the universe a time of birth in which it is born, and scattered the secrets of His universe among His creatures without revealing them all to one generation. Had the Qur'an revealed all its secrets to the unlettered nation contemporaneous with its revelation, they would have turned away from the new call by denying these matters, which minds would not accept even in the modern age and despite the advancement of the sciences. For example, when scholars spoke of the sphericity of the earth and its orbit around the sun, we did not believe these facts until the space photographs came to us confirming that.

We have said: the birth of a secret of the universe may coincide with a human inquiry, so the secret comes and appears as a result of that inquiry; otherwise Allah reveals it to people by chance, as a mercy to them and a bounty upon them. For this reason we find that most discoveries came by chance; humans did not seek them, nor did they arrive at them through premises.

When the noble Qur'an speaks of night and day, it says a general statement that every contemporary of every stage of scientific progress can understand: ﴿And We made the night and the day two signs…﴾ (12) [al-Isra'].

And He says: ﴿It is He who made the night and the day in succession for whoever wishes to remember or wishes to be grateful﴾ (62) [al-Furqan]. The meaning of "khilfah" (succession) is that one of them opposes the other and comes after it, and this is true now: we see the night following the day and the day following the night. But how do we conceive this matter at the beginning of creation?

If the beginning was that the earth was created facing the sun, then the day would be first, not a succession to anything before it; then the sun sets and the night arises to be a succession to the day. Conversely, if the earth were not facing the sun, then the night is first, not a succession to anything before it.

Therefore, this matter is resolved only by His saying: ﴿It is He who made the night and the day in succession…﴾ (62) [al-Furqan], that is, from the beginning of creation they were in succession. This is not possible or valid unless the earth is spherical, such that the part facing the sun constitutes the day and the other part the night at the same time. When the earth moved in its rotation, each became a succession to the other. Thus, the data of the Qur'an is digested by reason and never contradicts it.

You remember that in the 1930s, specifically in the year 1928, they interpreted the seven heavens as the seven wandering planets that revolve around the sun, in order to bring science closer to people. Allah, glorified be He, willed that afterwards they would discover Neptune and then Pluto, so they became nine planets, and Allah showed them the corruption of this interpretation.

There are many wonders in the universe that we know even through unbelievers; it is as though Allah subjected even the disbeliever to confirm the faith of the believer. If we have come to know today the day and night on earth, which make up twenty-four hours, what then does "day" mean for the other planets?

When they learned of the orbits of the other planets that revolve around the sun, they found the closest to the sun to be Mercury, then Venus, then Earth, then Mars, then Jupiter, then Saturn, then Neptune, then Pluto, which is the farthest of the planets from the sun.

Among the wonders of this day regarding these planets: a day on Venus, for example, equals 244 of our days, while its year equals 225 of our days. So a day on Venus is longer than its year. How? They said: because the orbit differs from the orbit of the Earth; the day is the result of the planet's rotation on its own axis, and the year is the result of the planet's revolution around the sun.

As for the saying of Allah: ﴿and He has subjected the sun and the moon…﴾ (29) [Luqman], you may notice the precision of the Qur'anic expression in the shift from the present tense ﴿causes ... to enter (yulij)﴾ (29) [Luqman] to the past ﴿subjected (sakhkhara)﴾ (29) [Luqman]. In speaking of the movement of night and day He said ﴿yulij﴾ (29) [Luqman], and when He spoke of the sun and the moon He said ﴿sakhkhara﴾ (29) [Luqman]. Why?

They said: because subjection occurred once, at one time, and then it became fixed; whereas the entering of night into day and of day into night is a continuous matter that recurs every day, so it suited the present tense, which indicates recurrence.

As for His saying: ﴿each running to a specified term (ajal musamma)﴾ (29) [Luqman], that is, to a limited goal. For this reason we call the final lifespan "ajal" (term), and the "specified term" is understood to be the Day of Resurrection. It is as though the Creator, glorified be He, has guaranteed us the continuation of the sun and the moon until the Hour arrives, so be at ease.

How great is this in a shining body that illuminates the whole world from the time Allah created it until the Hour, without maintenance and without spare parts. That is because it is built on compulsory subjection which precludes choice: the sun cannot refrain from rising, and likewise the moon. And among the greatness of divinity is this all-merciful compassion which embraces all, the believer in it and the disbeliever.

In this verse the expression ﴿ila ajalin musamma﴾ (29) [Luqman] is used, while in other places it is expressed as ﴿li-ajalin musamma﴾ (2) [al-Ra'd] with the lam instead of ila, and likewise in surahs Fatir (13) and al-Zumar (5). Each of the two particles has a meaning: ﴿ila ajalin﴾ (29) [Luqman] gives us the picture of the course of the sun and moon before they reach the term, whereas ﴿li-ajalin musamma﴾ (13) [Fatir] means the direct arrival at the term.

Just as the night has a function and the day has a function, so the sun has a function and the moon has a function, which Allah made clear in His saying: ﴿It is He who made the sun a radiance and the moon a light…﴾ (5) [Yunus].

In another place He, glorified be He, said: ﴿Blessed is He who placed in the sky constellations and placed therein a lamp and a luminous moon﴾ (61) [al-Furqan]. The radiance (diya') of the sun contains light and heat, unlike the light of the moon, which suits a dreamer and has no heat in it.

Among the wonders of the moon is that we used to think it was a piece of shining pearl in the sky, to the extent that poets were accustomed to comparing the beloved with the moon. Had they known the reality of the moon that we know today, that comparison would not have been valid for them. Science has informed us that the moon is nothing but stone and an opaque body that does not shine by itself, rather it only reflects the light of the sun. For this reason, when one poet compared his beloved to the moon, she rejected that resemblance from him:

I likened her to the full moon, so she laughed and met my words with denial

That is, she forced herself to laugh.

She ridiculed my saying and said: "When did I become so insipid that I have become like the full moon?"

And if you ask, how did you know the insipidness of the full moon, and that it is stone with no beauty in it? She answers when she says:

The full moon does not gaze with an eye as I gaze, nor does it smile with a mouth,

nor does it unveil the cloak from a swelling breast, nor does it tie the necklace at a throat.

Whoever measures my purity against the full moon, may my separation never cease to hold him captive in my hand.

So the reality of the moon that we have finally come to know is one of the signs of Allah, manifest and hidden, in the universe, which Allah has made us aware of through the authority of science. When it became possible for humans to ascend to its surface, we learned that it is an opaque body and rocks that do not shine by themselves, but reflect the rays of the sun, which reach us calm and dreamy. It is as though the moon, as they say, "makes sherbet out of fesikh" (a salted fish dish).

Among the wisdom of the Creator, glorified be He, in creating the sun and the moon is that the sun is a measure for knowing the day, and the moon for knowing the month, which is the basis for legal obligations, because it has a distinctive shape at the beginning of the month, unlike the sun. Therefore He, glorified be He, says: {It is He who made the sun a radiance and the moon a light and determined for it phases that you may know the number of years and the calculation}

1 Related by al-Bukhari in his Sahih (5624) and Ahmad in his Musnad (3/388) from Jabir ibn Abdullah; the wording is al-Bukhari's.

Then the Almighty says:

﴿That is because Allah is the Truth, and what they invoke besides Him is falsehood, and because Allah is the Most High, the Great.﴾ (31:30)

His saying, Exalted is He, ﴿That…﴾ refers to what was mentioned before: the entry of the night into the day, the entry of the day into the night, and the subjection of the sun and the moon. All of that is ﴿because Allah is the Truth.﴾ Everything mentioned earlier arises from one of the attributes of Allah, who is the Truth. The truth is that which is firm and does not change. So the order of the universe, with all its orbits and all the creatures within it, has a fixed system that does not change, because the One who created and originated it is the Truth. ﴿That is because Allah is the Truth.﴾

Since Allah, may He be exalted, is the (Truth), then what they invoke as partners are falsehood: ﴿and what they invoke besides Him is falsehood.﴾ There are not two truths in one thing. If one of them is the truth, then what is other than it is falsehood. Truth is one, and its opposite is falsehood. And what falsehood is more monstrous than their worship of idols, taking them as gods and partners with Allah, the Mighty and Majestic?

How could they do so, when they are stones that they fashioned with their own hands and set up to be worshipped besides Allah? Stones are inanimate matter of the earth, and inanimate matter is the first slave of all creatures: a slave to plants, a slave to animals, and a slave to humans, because it is subjected to serve all of these.

How, then, can you, O human, whom your Lord has honoured and given a thinking mind, degrade yourself and be content that it should worship the lowest kinds of existence and take it as a partner with Allah? You see that when the wind blows strongly, it knocks down al-Lat or al-'Uzza and throws it to the ground, and perhaps breaks its arm, so it needs someone to repair this god. Thus, ﴿what they invoke besides Him is falsehood.﴾

For this reason, we have said regarding the wars that break out between people: they do not break out between two truths, for truth does not contain two truths; there is only one truth, and the other must be falsehood, or they arise between two falsehoods. As for their arising between truth and falsehood, they generally do not last long, because falsehood is bound to vanish.

The final outcome must be for the truth, even if after a while. As for falsehood, it vanishes. A battle lengthens only if it breaks out between two falsehoods, for neither party is worthy of Allah's support, so the wars between them continue until both are exhausted, and the gains of each one's tyranny come to an end, and nothing turns them back except the humiliation of resorting to reconciliation after both have lost everything.

For this reason we also see this phenomenon in the distribution of estates and inheritances among those entitled to them, where disputes, slander, and resort to the courts and lawyers arise among them until all this consumes a large part of the estate. Then, when what was obtained by falsehood is cleared away, you see the parties inclining to agreement, reconciliation, and dividing what remains.

If you wish, read the saying of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ): "Whoever acquires wealth from *mahawish*, Allah will cause it to be lost in *nahabir*." The meaning of *mahawish*: by *al-tahwish*, or as we say (*bihabsh*), from here and from there. It is natural that Allah would cause this wealth to be lost in falsehood and in what has no benefit.

We have previously given an example of the outlets of unlawful money: a father returns home and finds his son ill with a high fever. He hurries him to the doctor and is struck with terror, and the specter of illness appears to him, so he spends hundreds on his son. But the one who lives on a modest living and toils to earn his livelihood lawfully will, in such a case, be satisfied with an aspirin tablet and a cup of lemon. The first one's wealth came from *mahawish*, and the other's came from what is lawful.

So Allah's saying, ﴿That is because Allah is the Truth,﴾ means: the truth is what is manifest and what prevails. If you say: how, when we see falsehood sometimes rising over the truth and prevailing over it? We say: yes, falsehood may rise, but only for a time, and in this state it is a soldier of the soldiers of truth. How? When falsehood rises and has its assault, it must bite people, harm them, and make them taste its calamities, so they turn to the truth, seek it, and yearn for it.

Thus, were it not for falsehood, we would not know the distinguishing quality of truth. An example of this is the pain that afflicts the human soul, alerting it to illness and revealing its cause, so it seeks the cure. Pain is thus a soldier of the soldiers of healing. We have said before that disbelief is a soldier of the soldiers of faith.

Therefore, do not grieve if you see falsehood rising high, for that is in the interest of the truth. Read the saying of your Lord, the Mighty and Majestic: ﴿He sends down water from the sky, and valleys flow according to their measure﴾ (13:17), meaning each valley takes of the water according to its capacity and size. ﴿So the torrent carries a foam that swells up﴾ (13:17), which is the chaff and debris the water carries. ﴿And from what they heat in the fire, seeking ornament or goods, there is a foam like it. Thus Allah strikes the parables of truth and falsehood﴾ (13:17), meaning, an illustration for each of them.

﴿As for the foam, it passes away as scum,﴾ (13:17), meaning cast out and removed from the trough. ﴿But as for what benefits people, it remains on the earth. Thus Allah sets forth parables﴾ (13:17).

After Allah, the Glorified and Exalted, explained that He is ﴿the Truth﴾ and that the other deities of the polytheists are falsehood, He mentioned two other attributes of Himself: ﴿and that Allah is the Most High, the Great﴾ (31:30). The Most High, the Great, is said by Allah, said by His Messenger (ﷺ), and said by us, because Allah said it, and because the truthful Prophet informed us of it. But the matter is that it is witnessed by one who disbelieves in Allah.

Therefore, our Lord, blessed and exalted, teaches us to praise Allah when the disbeliever bears witness to Allah despite his disbelief in Him, as occurred in the previous verse: ﴿If you asked them who created the heavens and the earth, they would surely say, "Allah." Say, "Praise be to Allah." But most of them do not know﴾ (31:25).

So this testimony from them deserves that the believer say, "Praise be to Allah," because it came from one who disbelieved in Allah, denied His Messenger, and fought against him. Also, consider this disbeliever who refuses the way of Allah and denies His Messenger: when illness strikes him, for example, can he refuse illness as he refused Allah? One who has accustomed himself to rebellion against Allah: will he rebel when death comes?

Read His saying, the Exalted: ﴿When harm touches you at sea, those you invoke vanish except Him﴾ (17:67), meaning that in the hour of distress and destruction they find before them none but Allah, for in that state a person does not deceive himself or lie to himself. By Allah, have you seen a person surrounded by waves, on the verge of destruction, calling out, "O Hubal!"? Thus: Allah is the Most High and the Great, and whatever else is associated with Him is polytheism and falsehood.

We have previously given an example of a person who does not cheat himself or deceive himself, especially when a distress befalls him, such as with the barber or the "health doctor," as they used to call him. He treats the people of the village and mocks the doctor of the health unit, accusing him of lacking experience. But when his child falls ill and he senses danger, he takes the child and slips away in the darkness of night, going to the doctor.

Supremacy belongs to Allah alone, and greatness belongs to Allah alone, as evidenced by the fact that when the disbeliever is compelled by life's circumstances and driven to a necessity from which there is no escape, he says nothing but, "O Allah, O my Lord."

So Allah is the Most High by the testimony of those who disbelieve in Him. Then He followed the attribute "the Most High" with the attribute "the Great," because "the Most High" might be understood as one who rose by tyranny and without deserving elevation. But the Most High, glorified is He, is the Most High, and He is the Great who deserves this loftiness.

Then the Truth, glory be to Him, draws our attention to another of His signs in the universe.

﴿Have you not seen that the ships sail through the sea by the favour of God, that He may show you some of His signs? Indeed in that are signs for every steadfast, grateful person.﴾ (31)

After mentioning some cosmic signs that are distant from us, He, glory be to Him, wished to give us another example of the signs that lie before us on the earth, so He said, exalted is He: ﴿Have you not seen that the ships sail through the sea by the favour of God..﴾ (31) [Luqman]. "Have you not seen" means: have you not known. ﴿That the ships..﴾ (31) [Luqman] means: the vessels.

Perhaps the Messenger of God did not see these ships on the seas, and the giant ships that we see today, like mountains, had not yet appeared, as in His saying, glory be to Him: ﴿And His are the ships, raised high on the sea like landmarks﴾ (24) [al-Rahman].

When did the towering battleships, resembling mountains and made up of several decks, come into existence? They only came into existence recently. Therefore, this is one of the manifestations of the miraculousness (i'jaz) of the Qur'an. Among such examples is His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And had it not been that people would become one community, We would have made for those who disbelieve in the Most Merciful silver roofs for their houses and stairways by which they ascend﴾ (33) [al-Zukhruf].

Whoever searches the Qur'an will find in it much of these signs that establish the truthfulness of the Qur'an and the truthfulness of the Messenger of God in conveying from God.

We have mentioned the story of the woman who embraced Islam when she read Islamic history and read in the biography of the Messenger of God that the believers in him used to keep a constant guard around him, taking turns to protect him from his enemies. Suddenly the Messenger of God dismissed these guards from around him and said to them: "God has revealed to me: ﴿And God will protect you from the people..﴾ (67) [al-Ma'idah]." The woman stopped at this verse and said: "By God, if this man were deceiving all people, he would not have deceived himself in his lifetime."

We have said regarding the meaning of ﴿Have you not seen..﴾ (31) [Luqman] that it means: have you not known, because God's informing you is more reliable than the sight of your eyes.

As for the phrase ﴿sail through the sea by the favour of God..﴾ (31) [Luqman]: al-jary (sailing) is a movement by which one transports oneself from one place to another; this transporting is either by walking slowly or by running. But what is God's favour in its sailing? First, the first ship was made of wood tied together with ropes and nails (al-dusur), and the part of it that sank into the water was about one span, displacing water equal in weight to the ship. So if you place a load on it, it sinks by the amount of that load, until, if the weight of the displaced water exceeds the weight of the ship and its cargo, it sinks.

This principle is the one used in submarines: by weight, the movement of the submarine under water is controlled. Now we see giant ships made of iron, and the wonder is that this solid iron is carried by soft flowing water and moves upon it. Then the wind comes and pushes the ships wherever they want, even if they travel against the direction of the water's flow. The ship's captain can control its movement using some simple instruments and by setting the sail in a particular way, so the ship goes as he wishes even if its direction is opposite to the direction of the wind. They call this movement (tasfih).

Therefore, He, glory be to Him, says regarding the movement of ships: ﴿If He wills, He calms the wind, and they become motionless on its surface..﴾ (33) [al-Shura].

It is as if the Truth, glory be to Him, wants to show us that the least dense things, by the power of the Truth, carry the most dense things. And consider, if you wish, heavy freight trucks: these giant trucks carrying several tons of iron, for example, on what do they move and travel? They move and travel on compressed air in their tyres, which takes its strength from this pressure, such that if you increase the pressure in these tyres beyond a point, they strengthen against themselves and burst.

As for His saying, ﴿that He may show you some of His signs..﴾ (31) [Luqman]: that is, of His wonders in His creation, especially in the seas. In the past we would see of the creatures in the depths only the fish that fishermen catch; but now, with the development of marine sciences and methods of underwater photography, we have come to see in the depths of the seas more wonders than we see on dry land.

Then He, exalted is He, says: ﴿Indeed in that are signs for every steadfast, grateful person.﴾ (31) [Luqman] His saying, ﴿for every steadfast..﴾ (31) [Luqman], suggests that God's signs in His creation are numerous, but man must exert effort in searching for them and discovering them, and he must be steadfast in the hardship of searching and diving beneath the water. So when we see the wonders of God's creatures in the depths of the seas, gratitude becomes incumbent upon us ﴿for every steadfast, grateful person.﴾ (31) [Luqman], and gratitude is only for a blessing that is newly renewed and did not exist before.

Thus, the Truth, blessed and exalted is He, wants us to receive His signs in the universe with inquiry, reflection and contemplation, not with heedlessness and aversion, as He, glory be to Him, said: ﴿And how many a sign in the heavens and the earth do they pass by, while they turn away from it!﴾ (105) [Yusuf].

And the placing of steadfast (sabbar) before grateful (shakur) is evidence that patience in the hardships of work, research, deduction and discovery brings a great blessing that calls a person to give thanks for it.

ThenAllah, the Exalted, says:

﴿And when a wave covers them like shadows, they call upon Allah, sincere to Him in religion. But when He delivers them to the land, some of them are moderate. And none deny Our signs except every treacherous ingrate.﴾ (32)

The meaning of ﴿غَشِيَهُم مَّوْجٌ﴾ [Luqman] (ghashiyahum mawj, "a wave covered them"): it means it covered them and enveloped them. Therefore He said ﴿كَالظُّلَلِ﴾ [Luqman] (ka-l-zulal, "like shadows"), plural of ẓullah, which is that which rises above a person and shades him.

A wave is not like this unless it rises above the level of a person and departs from the monotony and calm of water. Among this is the Exalted's saying: ﴿وَإِذْ نَتَقْنَا الْجَبَلَ فَوْقَهُمْ كَأَنَّهُ ظُلَّةٌ..﴾ (171) [Al-A'raf] ("And when We raised the mountain above them as though it were a canopy").

And you witness these phenomena if you are in the open sea: you see the wave from afar, higher than you, and that it will surely engulf you. Then, when it reaches you, you witness in it a manifestation of Allah's gentleness toward you, for it dissolves and passes beneath you in peace. This is a wonderful thing and a blessing that calls for gratitude.

So the wave is something frightening. Therefore, when it covered them and they were certain of destruction, ﴿دَعَوُا اللَّهَ مُخْلِصِينَ لَهُ الدِّينَ﴾ [Luqman] ("they called upon Allah, sincere to Him in religion"), they called upon Allah despite being disbelievers in Him. But a person in such a state does not deceive himself or lie to himself, for the matter is serious. So they did not call upon al-Lat or al-'Uzza, and none of them said "O Hubal." Rather, they called upon Allah with sincerity to Him. Even if they were inclined toward another religion in the worship of idols, in this situation they must be sincere to Allah, because they are certain that the idols will not benefit them, that they possess neither harm nor benefit for them, and that benefit and the removal of affliction come only from Allah, the Truth.

If you say: since the matter is so, what diverted them from worshiping Allah to worshiping idols?

We say: religiosity is a disposition in the human soul, and this disposition remains in the atoms of every human since Allah created Adam and took from his loins his offspring and made them testify concerning themselves: ﴿أَلَسْتُ بِرَبِّكُمْ..﴾ (172) [Al-A'raf] ("Am I not your Lord?"), and they testified.

Each one of us has an atom that witnessed this covenant, and this atom is the source of the illuminations in the soul of the believer. He must preserve it by taking the law of its preservation from the One who created it, and not extinguish its light by violating the law of its preservation which his Lord, Mighty and Majestic, has set for him. He would then be like the one of whom Allah said: ﴿وَمَنْ أَعْرَضَ عَنْ ذِكْرِي فَإِنَّ لَهُ مَعِيشَةً ضَنْكًا وَنَحْشُرُهُ يَوْمَ الْقِيَامَةِ أَعْمَى﴾ (124) [Ta-Ha] ("And whoever turns away from My remembrance, indeed, he will have a constricted life, and We will gather him on the Day of Resurrection blind").

The Prophet (ﷺ) clarifies this matter for us by his saying: "Every child is born upon the fitrah (natural disposition); then his parents make him a Jew, or a Christian, or a Magian."

The human soul is good as long as the first divine illuminations that witnessed that Allah is the Lord remain in it. But if it becomes clouded, disappointment must occur and corruption enters.

So: religiosity is a nature in the soul, but true religiosity has requirements and a method: "do this, and do not do that." This person wants to satisfy himself by being religious, but he wants to relieve himself of the requirements of this religiosity. So what does he do? He resorts to worshiping a god that has no requirements, and these were available in the worship of idols.

But we say to the one who worshiped idols: there must come a time when you will not turn to the idols, but to the true God from whose requirements you fled and whose worship you abandoned. Events must compel you to take refuge in Him. Therefore they say in the proverb: "The one you do not want to see his face, time will compel you to see his back."

You turned away from Allah and disbelieved in Him, but when events befell you and the waves surrounded you, you became rabbits. So why now do you turn to Allah? Why did you not persist in your obstinacy and arrogance even toward Allah?

Then He, the Exalted, says: ﴿فَلَمَّا نَجَّاهُمْ إِلَى الْبَرِّ فَمِنْهُم مُّقْتَصِدٌ..﴾ (32) [Luqman] ("But when He delivers them to the land, some of them are moderate"). After they had acknowledged that Allah is the true God to whom one turns and by whom one seeks help, and after He had saved and relieved them, they should have believed in Him, obeyed Him, and let this shaking that convulsed them leave its effect upon them. Yet they returned to what they had been upon of disbelief and turning away from Allah, and obeyed their souls and desires.

This is the condition of the disbeliever when he is subjected to trial and testing: he relapses and does not recover, unlike the believer, who, if he is subjected to such a test, increases in faith and certainty.

The moderate (muqtasid) is the one who is between two states: events and calamities seize him and return him to Allah in time of distress and hardship, but when it is lifted from him he wavers and this spirit weakens in him. The evidence is that Allah, the Exalted, mentions, in contrast to the moderate, another kind of them who are not moderate: ﴿وَمَا يَجْحَدُ بِآيَاتِنَا إِلَّا كُلُّ خَتَّارٍ كَفُورٍ﴾ (32) [Luqman] ("And none deny Our signs except every treacherous ingrate").

Among them is one whose disbelief subsides when the faith-driven restraint within him is awakened, but when he is saved, the world deceives him anew. And among them is the one who denies, the khattar, i.e., the treacherous.

You may also notice the contrast between ṣabbar (steadfast, patient) and khattar (treacherous), and between shakur (grateful) and kafur (ungrateful).

Then Allah, glorified is He, addresses people, saying:

﴿O mankind, fear your Lord, and dread a Day when no parent will avail his child at all, nor will a child avail his parent in anything. Indeed, the promise of Allah is true. So do not let the worldly life delude you, and do not let the Deceiver delude you concerning Allah.﴾ (33)

The address of the Truth, glorified is He, to His servants with "O mankind" shows that He, the Exalted, wishes to make them all happy in the Hereafter. We have previously mentioned the divine hadith (hadith qudsi, a saying of Allah reported by the Prophet ﷺ) in which the earth says, "O Lord, permit me to swallow the son of Adam," and the seas say, "Let us drown him," and so on. The response from the Creator, Mighty and Majestic, was: "Leave them to Me and My creation. If you had created them, you would have shown them mercy. If they repent to Me, I am their beloved; and if they do not repent, I am their physician."

His saying, Exalted is He, ﴿Fear your Lord...﴾ [Luqman] (33). Taqwa (God-consciousness, fear of Allah) is that you place between yourself and what harms you a protection that guards and shields you. For this reason, He says in another verse, ﴿and fear the Fire﴾ [Al 'Imran] (131). The two have one meaning, because the meaning of "fear Allah" is: place between yourselves and the attributes of the majesty of your Lord, His retribution and His might, a protection. The same applies to "fear the Fire."

Here the address is general to all people, believers and disbelievers alike. Allah, Exalted is He, wishes to bring them all into the sphere of faith and obedience, and wishes to give them, bestow favour upon them, and help them. It is as if He, glorified is He, were saying to them: "I do not want for you only the blessings of this world; rather I want to give you also the bliss of the Hereafter."

Likewise was the Prophet ﷺ, who was merciful even toward the disbelievers and those who opposed him, as we mentioned in the story of the Jew whom they falsely accused of stealing the coat of mail (dir') of one of the Muslims. It was grievous to the Muslims that one of them should be accused of theft, so they placed it with the Jew and referred the matter to our master, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, who turned it over in his mind: how should he deal with it?

Allah granted him success and revealed to him: ﴿Indeed, We have sent down to you the Book in truth, that you may judge between the people by what Allah has shown you﴾ [An-Nisa'] (105), not only between believers. ﴿And do not be an advocate for the treacherous﴾ [An-Nisa'] (105), meaning: do not argue on behalf of the traitor, even if he is a Muslim. All people are equal before the responsibility of faith.

There is a difference between "fear your Lord" and "fear Allah," because the bounty of lordship (rububiyyah, Allah's role as Creator, Sustainer and Nurturer) is not the same as the bounty of divinity (uluhiyyah, the right to be worshipped). The bounty of lordship is bringing into existence from non-existence, sustaining from non-existence, and nurturing both believer and disbeliever. The bounty of divinity is obedience, worship, and carrying out of commands. Here He chose "your Lord," who created and nurtured. It is as if He, glorified is He, were saying to all people: "It is incumbent upon you to make the fear of Allah a thanks for His favour upon you, even if you have disbelieved in it."

The matter does not end with fearing the Lord in this world; rather, ﴿and dread a Day when no parent will avail his child at all...﴾ [Luqman] (33). That is: fear a Day on which you will return to your Lord. The word "day" (yawm) can be used as an adverb of time, and it can be used as an independent noun. It is an adverb when an event will occur on that day, as you say: "I feared the severity of the scrutiny on the day of the exam," so the fear is of the event, not of the day itself. But if you say, "I feared the day of the exam," then the fear is of everything in that day, that is, of the day itself.

So the meaning here, ﴿and dread a Day...﴾ [Luqman] (33), is that the day itself is frightening regardless of the recompense in it. On this Day, ﴿no parent will avail his child at all...﴾ [Luqman] (33). The parent and child are singled out here because He, glorified is He, advised everyone, and then singled out the parents in the well-known charge: ﴿And We have enjoined upon man concerning his parents...﴾ [Luqman] (14).

Then He mentioned the grounds for this charge and said: ﴿Give thanks to Me and to your parents...﴾ [Luqman] (14). Thus He gave them virtue, distinction and rank with Allah, to the extent that they became a source of benefit even until the Day of Resurrection. Allah, glorified is He, wished to make clear to us that the benefit of a parent to his child ends in the Hereafter, for each of them is preoccupied with himself, so a person is not benefited even by those closest to him.

In Surat al-Baqarah: ﴿And fear a Day when no soul will avail another soul at all...﴾ [Al-Baqarah] (48). That is, any soul at all, not only parent and child. Rather, people in general, none of them will benefit another, whoever he may be.

This verse in this wording occurs in two places. They agree in the beginning and differ in the end, and it speaks of two souls: the first is the soul that avails (jazi), that is, the one that bears the recompense; the other is the soul that is availed for (majzi 'anha), the one deserving punishment.

The verse that considers the soul for which recompense is made ends with ﴿No ransom will be accepted from it, nor will intercession benefit it﴾ [Al-Baqarah] (123).

By "adl" is meant ransom (fidyah). The first stage for the soul that is to be recompensed, to ward off punishment from itself, is to offer ransom, but it is not accepted from it. Yet it does not despair; rather it seeks someone of standing and rank who will intercede for it with Allah, and this too does not benefit it.

As for the soul that avails, the first thing offered to it is intercession, and if that is not accepted, ransom is offered. Therefore the end of the other verse, which considers the soul that avails, places intercession before ransom. So: the end of the first verse refers to the soul that is availed for, and the end of the second verse refers to the soul that avails.

Here ﴿no parent will avail his child...﴾ [Luqman] (33), because the parent is the seat of tenderness toward the child. When a parent sees his child suffering, he wants to ransom him. So "parent" is mentioned first here, then He said: ﴿nor will a child avail his parent in anything...﴾ [Luqman] (33), placing "child" (mawlud) after. The expected wording would have been: "nor will a child (walad) avail his parent." So why did He turn from "walad" to "mawlud"?

The speech here is the speech of the Lord, and there is a great difference between walad and mawlud. The early Muslims had fathers who died in disbelief, and they thought that Allah's charge concerning parents permitted them to avail on their behalf on the Day of Resurrection. So Allah revealed this verse to show them that they should not hope to ward off anything from their fathers who died in disbelief.

Therefore He did not say "walad" here, but "mawlud," because the mawlud is the one directly born of the parent, whereas walad is applied to the grandfather and whoever is higher. Thus the grandfather too is a "walad" of his grandson, and the grandson's father is his "walad." If intercession is not accepted from a mawlud for his direct parent, it is all the more so not accepted for a grandfather. So He turned from walad to mawlud. The matter is the speech of a wise Lord, not mere arrangement of words.

But when does a parent avail for a child, and a child for his parent? They said: the child is weak in relation to his parent, needing affection and care from him, so when the parent sees his child suffering, he hastens to intercede for him and to remove the pain from him. But the child does not remove pain from his father, because he is grown; rather he averts humiliation. So the parent intercedes regarding suffering, and the child intercedes regarding humiliation. Each of them has its station.

Then He, glorified is He, says: ﴿Indeed, the promise of Allah is true...﴾ [Luqman] (33). We know that a promise (wa'd) is news of something pleasing that has not yet come at its time, and its opposite is a threat (wa'id), which is news of something painful that has not yet come at its time. But what is the benefit of each?

The benefit of a promise is that you prepare for it and take up its causes. It encourages you to work and strive to achieve this promise, as when you promise your son, for example, a reward if he succeeds in the exam. The threat, on the contrary, frightens you of its consequence so that you take precautions and take up the means of salvation from it.

So: the promise is true, and likewise the threat is true. But He singled out the promise because it brings to the soul what it loves, whereas the threat may prevent it from a desire it loves. We have clarified this point: the Truth, glorified is He, speaks of blessings, that among them are blessings of bestowal and blessings of withdrawal.

Read in this regard the saying of your Lord: ﴿There will be sent against you both a flame of fire and smoke, and you will not be able to defend yourselves. So which of the favours of your Lord would you deny?﴾ [Ar-Rahman] (35-36).

If Paradise and what is in it are blessings deserving thanks, with which Allah bestows favour upon us, then what blessing is there in the flame, the fire and the punishment? They said: it is a blessing in that it is a warning and an admonition against punishment, so that you keep away from its causes and are saved from it before you fall into it. It is a blessing because Allah did not seize us unawares, and alerted us to the danger before we fell into it.

The promise of Allah is true, because it is a promise from One who possesses the ability to fulfil what He promised and to carry out what He promised. But other than Allah, glorified is He, does not possess the means of fulfilment, so his promise cannot be described as true. For this reason He, glorified is He, said in Surat al-Kahf: ﴿And never say of anything, "Indeed, I will do that tomorrow," except [adding], "If Allah wills"...﴾ [Al-Kahf] (23-24).

So even if you are sincere about what you promised, you cannot guarantee remaining alive to fulfil it. If you remain, circumstances may change and come between you and fulfilment, and you do not possess a single one of these causes.

So: be courteous, and leave the matter to the One who possesses all the means of carrying out the promise, and say, "I will do so-and-so, if Allah wills," so that if you do not carry it out, you will have an excuse, and say: "I intended it, but Allah did not will it."

It is as if our Lord, Mighty and Majestic, wishes to cover up our lying and conceal it from us. He wants not to disgrace us by it, and He removed us from this responsibility by leaving the will to Him, glorified is He. It is as if the decree of Allah concerning things is a safeguard for His servants from His servants. Therefore we often say when we cannot fulfil something: "This is the decree of Allah, and what can I do? The matter is not decided on earth until it is decided in heaven."

Since we have believed in the decree of Allah and its wisdom, do not be angry with me if I do not keep my word to you, and you likewise. The wise person knows full well, when he decides a matter for someone, that the decision comes with him, not through him. Decree is a judgement, and his judgement agrees with Allah's judgement of the matter, so it is as though Allah honoured him by having the matter decided through his hands. Therefore we have said: the believing physician says, "The cure came with me, not through me," and that the physician treats while Allah heals. So: the promise is not described as true except the promise of Allah, Mighty and Majestic.

Since the promise of Allah is true, you must do what He promised reward for, avoid what He threatened punishment for, and not let worldly life delude you: ﴿So do not let the worldly life delude you...﴾ [Luqman] (33). That is, by its adornment and its decoration, for it is a deceptive mirage with nothing behind it. Read the saying of Allah, Exalted: ﴿Did you then think that We created you uselessly and that you would not be returned to Us?﴾ [Al-Mu'minun] (115).

The Truth, glorified is He, sets forth for us a parable of the worldly life, not to repel us from it, but so that we may be cautious in approaching it. Otherwise, love of life is a desirable matter insofar as it is a field for working for the Hereafter and an arena for racing toward it.

He, Exalted, says regarding this parable: ﴿And present to them the example of the worldly life...﴾ [Al-Kahf] (45). He named it "dunya" (the lowest, nearer), and there is no description more eloquent in belittling it than that it is "dunya." ﴿Like water which We send down from the sky, and the plants of the earth mingle with it, but then it becomes dry remains scattered by the winds...﴾ [Al-Kahf] (45). Yes, thus the worldly life glitters, but it quickly passes away. It begins with a convincing and enticing beginning, and it ends with a regrettable ending.

His saying, Exalted: ﴿And let not the Deceiver deceive you concerning Allah﴾ [Luqman] (33). The "ghurur" (with fatha) is the one who deceives you about something. The meaning of "ghurur" is made clear to us by the pre-Islamic poet addressing his beloved:

"O Fatima, enough, some of this coquetry;
and if you have resolved to cut me off, then be gracious.
Does it delude you that your love is my killer,
and that whatever you command, the heart will do?"

So the meaning of "gharraka" (he deceived you) is: he has entered into you with delusion, such that you turn toward things and act regarding them within the shelter of this delusion and by its light.

"Al-Gharur" (with fatha) is Satan, and in his deception he has ways and varieties: deception for the obedient and deception for the disobedient. Each has a specific entry point. He deceives the disobedient through disobedience, and whispers to him that Allah is Forgiving and Merciful, and that his father disobeyed and Allah forgave him. Therefore one of the righteous, hearing the saying of Allah, Exalted: { O mankind, ...

Then the Truthful Lord, concluding Surat Luqman, says:

﴿Indeed, Allah has with Him knowledge of the Hour, and He sends down the rain, and He knows what is in the wombs. No soul knows what it will earn tomorrow, and no soul knows in what land it will die. Indeed, Allah is All-Knowing, All-Aware.﴾ (31:34)

After warning us, may our Lord, blessed and exalted, be He, against delusion in the life of this world, He reminds us that after this life there is another life, a resurrection and an Hour: ﴿Indeed, Allah has with Him knowledge of the Hour..﴾ (31:34). The Hour does not mean only the Resurrection; rather, each of us has his own hour, for whoever dies, his resurrection has come.

Why? Because his deeds have ceased, and he cannot make up for what he missed of faith or righteous deeds, so it is as if his resurrection occurred at his death.

We have also said: the age of the world, for you, is the measure of your lifetime in it. Even if the age of the world in reality is from Adam, peace be upon him, until the establishment of the Hour, what benefit have you gained from the lifespan of others?

Therefore, you should not say that the world is long, for your time in it is short, and moreover you do not know it, nor can you control it. Just as Allah concealed the hour, He concealed the term (ajal), for in its concealment is the most beneficial clarification. When Allah concealed the term, He made the human soul watch for it at every moment; every moment that passes over you, death may come to you in it.

Thus He spread death throughout all time. Since this is the case, a person must pay heed and fear dying while in disobedience, so the concealment here is itself the clarification.

We have also said: those who died from Adam, peace be upon him, onward remain in their graves throughout this whole period. Then, when the Resurrection comes: ﴿As if, on the day they see it, they had not remained except for an evening or its morning.﴾ (79:46) Why? They said: because the measuring of time is only possible through events, so where there are no events, there is no time.

We illustrated this with the People of the Cave, who remained in their cave three hundred years and added nine. Yet when some of them asked others: ﴿How long have you remained?' They said: 'We have remained a day or part of a day..﴾ (18:19)

Why? Because sleep is empty of events, so the sleeper does not perceive time. Likewise, when they saw one another after this period, each saw the other in the state in which he had slept, unaffected by the passage of this duration, and his appearance had not changed. So the most one could imagine is that he would say: "We remained a day or part of a day."

The same is the case in the story of Uzair, about whom Allah said: ﴿Or like the one who passed by a town that was fallen upon its roofs. He said: 'How will Allah bring this to life after its death?' So Allah caused him to die for a hundred years, then resurrected him. He said: 'How long have you remained?' He said: 'I have remained a day or part of a day..﴾ (2:259) — because this is the longest period a person can sleep.

Then his Lord informed him: ﴿Rather, you have remained a hundred years..﴾ (2:259). The Truthful Lord wishes to demonstrate the man's truthfulness in his saying "a day or part of a day," and His own truthfulness in saying "a hundred years," so He says: ﴿Look at your food and your drink, it has not spoiled..﴾ (2:259), meaning, it has not changed.

This is evidence of his truthfulness regarding a day or part of a day. ﴿And look at your donkey..﴾ (2:259).

And this is evidence of the truthfulness of the Blessed and Exalted Lord in His saying ﴿a hundred years..﴾ (2:259). So both statements are true, because Allah is the One who withholds and extends (al-Qabid al-Basit); He contracts time for some people and extends it for others.

This verse gathers five matters whose knowledge Allah has reserved for Himself: ﴿Indeed, Allah has with Him knowledge of the Hour, and He sends down the rain, and He knows what is in the wombs. No soul knows what it will earn tomorrow, and no soul knows in what land it will die..﴾ (31:34).

So are these all the unseen matters in the universe? We say: the universe contains many unseen matters that we do not know, but these five are surely what was asked about, and the answer was in proportion to the question. By Allah, if the wind blew and carried some sand with it, would we know where those particles went, and in what direction? Would we know how many leaves of the trees have fallen?

These are all unseen matters that none knows but Allah. As for us, we do not even know the number of the blessings Allah has bestowed upon us: ﴿And if you tried to count the favor of Allah, you could not enumerate it..﴾ (14:34).

So these are examples of what Allah has reserved for His knowledge, for Allah the Exalted says: ﴿And if whatever trees on earth were pens and the sea, replenished by seven more seas after it, the words of Allah would not be exhausted. Indeed, Allah is Almighty, All-Wise.﴾ (31:27).

So Allah, the Exalted, has in His universe secrets that cannot be counted; Allah has deferred their coming into being, so that we know that every day we are ignorant of what is with Allah, and every day scholars and researchers reveal to us something new of the secrets of this universe while we are still in this world. What then of the Hereafter, and of Paradise, God willing?

The Prophet ﷺ has informed us about it, saying: "In it is what no eye has seen, no ear has heard, and no human heart has conceived."

A person acquires knowledge either by sight of the eye or hearing of the ear. It is known that the scope of hearing is wider than that of sight, for you see only what your eyes see, but you hear the reports of others. Moreover, you hear and see what exists; but there is what has never occurred to a human heart, meaning unseen things that have not crossed anyone's mind. Concerning this, He says: ﴿No soul knows what has been hidden for them of comfort for eyes as a reward for what they used to do.﴾ (32:17)

It is reported in the occasions of revelation of these keys to the unseen that a man from Muharib, named al-Harith ibn Amr ibn Harithah, came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and said: "O Messenger of Allah, I want to know when the Hour will be. I have sown my seed and I await rain, so when will it fall? My wife is pregnant and I want her to bear a male. I have prepared for today its provision, so what should I prepare for tomorrow? I know the place of my life; how can I know the place of my death?"

These are five specific matters, and the answer to them came from Allah, the Exalted: ﴿Indeed, Allah has with Him knowledge of the Hour, and He sends down the rain, and He knows what is in the wombs. No soul knows what it will earn tomorrow, and no soul knows in what land it will die..﴾ (31:34).

It is strange that some of Allah's creation try to override what Allah has said regarding these five unseen matters, like those who tried to predict the time of the Hour's establishment, and all of them lied. Had they been granted faith in Allah and knowledge of what Allah said about the establishment of the Hour, none of them would have dared to address this question.

We have also said: Allah the Truthful concealed the appointed time of the Hour so that we would always sense it, at every time, even those who do not believe in it and doubt it. When people sense it, they act for it and prepare for its terrors, just as Allah concealed from man the hour of his death and the place of his term, and made death revolve among the servants without a fixed rule.

Some die minutes after birth, and some live hundreds of years. Moreover, He, glorified, did not make for death any preliminaries of sickness or otherwise: how many a patient recovers and how many a healthy person dies. As they say: "How is your patient?" He said: "Our healthy one died." And the poet spoke truly:

So do not consider illness a cup of death,
even if it is a sickness of severe effect.
For many a sick person you see recovers,
and many a healthy person you see is taken.

Likewise death is not tied to age:

How many a tender young maiden was taken, and her old mother was left behind.
It may be that the fates delay, but eternity in this world is not permitted.

So: Allah concealed the Resurrection and concealed death, so that we remain mindful of Him, expecting Him at every moment, and so that we act for Him, and always expect that we shall meet Allah, and prepare for the matter its preparation, for whoever has died, his resurrection has come, because his deeds have ceased. In the concealment of the appointed time of the Resurrection and the hour of death lies the very clarification of each of them; the concealment has spread it at every time.

As for His saying ﴿And He sends down the rain..﴾ (31:34): this too, and despite the advance of sciences, some have tried to predict it on the basis of precise calculations of wind speed, temperature, and so on. Perhaps their calculations were correct, but they overlooked that Allah has decrees in the universe that occur and do not enter their calculations; often we are surprised by a change in temperature or the direction of the wind, and all our calculations are overturned.

Therefore, among the wonders of creation: the closer you get to the sun, the source of heat, the lower the temperature becomes, and the farther you move from it, the higher the temperature rises. So the matter is not routine; it is a power of Allah, and Allah gathers the causes for you to establish the absoluteness of His power, which says to a thing: "Be," and it is.

Are we not commanded in the Hajj to kiss one stone and throw at another, and each is an act of faith and obedience? This one is trodden upon, that one is kissed, this one is kissed and that one is pelted. Why? Because Allah wants us to submit to His command, and for the believing soul to submit to the Lord who gives life and who imposes obligations.

As for His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿And He knows what is in the wombs..﴾ (31:34): this too is among the keys to the unseen, and it will remain so however far knowledge advances, and however much creatures claim that they know what is in the wombs. What has created a problem in this matter now is the modern devices by which they have been able to see the fetus and determine its sex, male or female. This scientific step has caused confusion among some people, who imagined that physicians know what is in the wombs, and on that basis they thought this matter is no longer among the keys to the unseen that Allah has reserved.

We say: by the authority of knowledge you know what is in the wombs after it has formed, its features have become clear, and its creation completed. But the Creator, Mighty and Majestic, knows what is in the wombs before the mother conceives it. Did Allah not give good news to His Prophet Zakariyya, peace be upon him, of his son Yahya before his wife conceived him? We do not know this unseen by our own selves, but only by what Allah has taught us. So the physician who tells you the sex of the fetus does not know the unseen; rather, he is a teacher of the unseen.

Allah, blessed and exalted, reveals to some of creation some unseen matters. Among these is what happened with the Companion Abu Bakr, may Allah be pleased with him, when he charged his daughter Aisha, may Allah be pleased with her, before he died, saying: "O Aisha, they are only your two brothers and two sisters." Aisha was surprised, since she had no siblings besides Muhammad and Abd al-Rahman, and of sisters only Asma. But Abu Bakr at that time was married to the daughter of Kharijah, who was pregnant, and after his death she bore him a daughter. So shall we say that Abu Bakr knew the unseen? No, he knew it from Allah. So what is forbidden here is independent knowledge, that you know by your own self.

Moreover, the physician now knows the sex of the fetus, either from an X-ray image or from tests he performs on a sample of the fetus, and this is not considered knowledge of the unseen. The "cleverness" is for a pregnant woman to sit before you and you say to her: "You, God willing, will give birth to such-and-such," and this never happens.

Then He, glorified, says: ﴿And no soul knows what it will earn tomorrow..﴾ (31:34). A person works either for his worldly life or for his Hereafter. So the meaning is either he earns worldly good for his own self to live, or, if it concerns moral obligation, the soul either does good or evil, a good deed or an evil one, and in his life a human being is subject to change.

Therefore it is said in a tradition: "O son of Adam, do not ask Me for tomorrow's provision, just as I did not demand of you tomorrow's deed."

As for His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿And no soul knows in what land it will die..﴾ (31:34): there has been a problem with this matter, because the Messenger of Allah ﷺ informed the Ansar that he would die in Medina, while alive
